item.title: Exploring sex differences in global cancer incidence and mortality and the role of national development level.
item.dc:creator: Hoveling LA, Bergink-Voorthuis BJ, van Vlaardingen JRG, Verhoeven RHA, Wagner AD, Soerjomataram I, Siesling S
item.description:
Authors: Hoveling LA, Bergink-Voorthuis BJ, van Vlaardingen JRG, Verhoeven RHA, Wagner AD, Soerjomataram I, Siesling S
Journal: ESMO real world data and digital oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.esmorw.2026.100790
Published: 2026-Dec-01
PMID: 42959695



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We analysed sex differences in global cancer incidence and mortality using a national development index to better understand how broader socioeconomic factors may contribute to or mitigate sex differences in cancer outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Cancer incidence and mortality data (2012-2017) were obtained from the International Agency for Research on Cancer, covering 43 countries for incidence and 60 for mortality. Only nonsex-specific cancers were included and categorised into 12 groups. Age-standardised incidence rates (ASIR) and age-standardised mortality rates (ASMRs) were calculated, with sex differences analysed using men-to-women ratios (MWRs). Linear regression was used to assess the association between Human Development Index (HDI) and MWRs across cancer types. RESULTS: Among the cancer types included in this study, cancers of the colorectum, stomach, and lungs showed the highest incidence and mortality. Men are 12-13 times more likely to be diagnosed with oesophageal cancer (MWR ≈ 13), over nine times more likely to die from head and neck cancers, and >6 times more likely to die from lung cancer. Thyroid cancer incidence is up to five times higher in women than in men. No clear link was found between HDI and MWRs in incidence, but HDI relates to mortality and MWRs for several cancer types, with brain and thyroid cancers showing higher male mortality, while lung cancer showing relatively higher female mortality in high-HDI countries. CONCLUSIONS: Sex differences in cancer burden vary substantially across cancer types. National development was associated with sex differences in mortality, but not incidence, suggesting that factors related to health care and survival differ more between countries with different HDIs and contribute to these differences more than exposure to risk factors, which relates more to incidence.

item.title: A multicenter, prospective, phase 2 trial on proton re-irradiation for patients with previously treated head and neck cancer.
item.dc:creator: Dee EC, Barker CA, Kalman NS, Wu Y, White C, Zhang Z, Lin H, Gelblum DY, Yu Y, Kang JJ, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Dee EC, Barker CA, Kalman NS, Wu Y, White C, Zhang Z, Lin H, Gelblum DY, Yu Y, Kang JJ, et al.
Journal: Cancer | DOI: 10.1002/cncr.70643
Published: 2026-Nov-01
PMID: 42963935



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Re-irradiation (re-RT) for recurrent head and neck cancer (HNC) can be potentially curative but is constrained by significant toxicity. Proton therapy may improve the therapeutic ratio. This multicenter phase 2 trial evaluated the safety and efficacy of proton re-RT in patients with HNC. METHODS: Patients received prior HNC radiotherapy at a dose of ≥40 gray (Gy). Salvage surgery and/or systemic therapy before re-RT were permitted. Considering clinical status, two pragmatic treatment approaches were used: fractionated re-RT (F-Re-RT; 60-70 Gy) or QUAD shot re-RT (QS-Re-RT; 14.8 Gy per cycle, up to four cycles; maximum total, 59.2 Gy). Primary end points were locoregional recurrence-free rates at 12 months for F-Re-RT and at 6 months for QS-Re-RT, and a fixed-time, binary proportion analyzed using 90% Clopper-Pearson confidence intervals (CIs) and prespecified success thresholds (lower bound, >55% and >10%, respectively). Secondary end points included overall survival (OS), progression-free survival, the cumulative incidence of distant metastasis and locoregional recurrence, clinician-reported toxicity, and patient-reported outcomes. RESULTS: From July 2017 to November 2022, 85 patients received either F-Re-RT (n = 57) or QS-Re-RT (n = 28), with a median follow-up of 38 months. The locoregional recurrence-free rates were 71% (90% CI, 59%-81%) at 12 months for F-Re-RT and 76% (90% CI, 58%-89%) at 6 months for QS-Re-RT, surpassing prespecified success thresholds. The highest late toxicity attributable to re-RT was grade 3 in 20% of patients, grade 4 in 11%, and grade 5 in 4%. The 5-year OS rate was 29%, and the 5-year progression-free survival rate was 23%. Patient-reported outcomes were stable at 1 year after F-Re-RT and after QS-Re-RT. CONCLUSIONS: Proton re-RT demonstrated encouraging locoregional control and survival in heavily pretreated patients, although late toxicities remain important concerns (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03217188).

item.title: Curative-intent management of de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma: an evidence-based consensus guideline from the International Collaborating Oncology Organisations.
item.dc:creator: Guo QJ, Liu Q, Bossi P, Bonomo P, Colevas AD, Lee NY, Lu TZ, Lee V, Mehanna H, Ng WT, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Guo QJ, Liu Q, Bossi P, Bonomo P, Colevas AD, Lee NY, Lu TZ, Lee V, Mehanna H, Ng WT, et al.
Journal: The Lancet. Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/S1470-2045(26)00347-5
Published: 2026-Nov-01
PMID: 42933448



Abstract:
Patients with de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma were historically deemed incurable and treated with palliative intent. Emergence of potent systemic therapy in combination with local treatment for both locoregional and metastatic diseases has enabled long-term survival in some patients. This international guideline was developed through consensus-building by 54 experts from 46 centres across 18 countries or regions and endorsed by 17 oncology organisations. 32 recommendations across seven clinical domains were formulated, including 29 strong (≥80% agreement [consensus] or high quality of evidence) and three conditional recommendations (67-79% agreement). We recommend that curative-intent treatment should be offered to medically fit patients with no more than three metastatic lesions in two or fewer organs at baseline or following response to systemic therapy; multimodality treatment (comprising immunochemotherapy, locoregional radiotherapy, metastasis-directed therapy, and maintenance therapy) is recommended. This guideline provides a practical framework for standardisation of clinical management of de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma and identification of key evidence gaps for future research.

item.title: Neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and chemotherapy versus standard of care for locally advanced rectal cancer (UNION): a prespecified interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial.
item.dc:creator: Tao K, Lin Z, Zhang P, Chi P, Xiao Y, Hou Z, Xu X, Zhang A, Qiu X, Wu J, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Tao K, Lin Z, Zhang P, Chi P, Xiao Y, Hou Z, Xu X, Zhang A, Qiu X, Wu J, et al.
Journal: The Lancet. Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/S1470-2045(26)00446-8
Published: 2026-Nov-01
PMID: 42927765



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To our knowledge, UNION is the first phase 3 trial to assess a neoadjuvant strategy incorporating radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and chemotherapy compared with standard care in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, which reported positive results for the primary endpoint (blinded independent review committee [BIRC]-assessed pathological complete response rate; 39·8% vs 15·3%). Here, we present a prespecified interim analysis of event-free survival. METHODS: This open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial was conducted at nine hospitals in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years with untreated cT3-4 or N+ rectal adenocarcinoma (≤10 cm distance from the anal verge) and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1; stratified by clinical T stage and N stage), using permuted blocks, to receive neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy (25 Gy in five fractions) followed by two cycles of intravenous camrelizumab (200 mg on day 1) plus CAPOX (oral capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1-14 and intravenous oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 on day 1; experimental group) or long-course chemoradiotherapy (50·4 Gy in 28 fractions with concurrent oral capecitabine 825 mg/m2 twice daily) followed by two cycles of CAPOX (standard-of-care group). After surgery, both groups received six cycles of adjuvant CAPOX, and the experimental group additionally received adjuvant camrelizumab for up to 15 cycles. The primary endpoint was BIRC-assessed pathological complete response rate in the intention-to-treat population, which has been previously reported. Here, we performed a prespecified interim analysis of investigator-assessed event-free survival (one of the key secondary endpoints, defined as time from randomisation to radiographic progression precluding surgery, local recurrence or distant metastasis, or death) in the intention-to-treat population (all randomly assigned patients) with a boundary of a two-sided p values less than 0·0102. Safety was evaluated in all patients who received at least one dose of the study treatment according to the assigned regimen. The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04928807, and is active, but no longer recruiting. FINDINGS: Between July 23, 2021, and March 1, 2023, 231 patients (153 [66%] males and 78 [34%] females; 227 [98%] were Han Chinese, and four [2%] were other ethnicity Chinese) were randomly assigned to the experimental group (n=113) and standard-of-care group (n=118). As of Oct 1, 2025, the median follow-up duration was 36·7 months (IQR 32·6-39·9) in the experimental group and 34·7 months (31·1-39·1) in the standard-of-care group. The 3-year investigator-assessed event-free survival rate was 91·3% (95% CI 83·9-95·4) in the experimental group versus 77·4% (67·9-84·4) in the standard-of-care group (stratified hazard ratio 0·33 [0·15-0·71]; two-sided log-rank p=0·0029). During the entire treatment period, the most common grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were decreased lymphocyte count (23 [20%] of 115 in the experimental group vs 31 [28%] of 112 in the standard-of-care group), decreased white blood cell count (13 [11%] vs 16 [14%]), decreased neutrophil count (13 [11%] vs 13 [12%]), and decreased platelet count (seven [6%] vs 15 [13%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 22 (19%) versus 15 (13%) patients, with the most common being decreased platelet count (one [1%] vs six [5%]), and radiation gastroenteritis (two [2%] vs four [4%]). Treatment-related deaths occurred in one patient in the experimental group (septic shock related to chemotherapy, but unrelated to camrelizumab) and none in the standard-of-care group. INTERPRETATION: In this interim analysis, short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and CAPOX significantly improved 3-year event-free survival in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, with a safety profile similar to long-course chemoradiotherapy followed by CAPOX. Comparison of this promising new treatment strategy with contemporary total neoadjuvant therapy strategies is warranted. FUNDING: Key Clinical Research Initiative Program of Union Hospital, National Key Technology Research and Development Programme of Hubei Province, and Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals. TRANSLATION: For the Chinese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

item.title: Cancer in Seychelles: A Population-Based Study on Incidence, Trends and Stage at Diagnosis (2005-2024).
item.dc:creator: Finesse A, Mondon J, Shroff E, Gedeon J, Louange M, Parkin DM
item.description:
Authors: Finesse A, Mondon J, Shroff E, Gedeon J, Louange M, Parkin DM
Journal: International journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1002/ijc.70769
Published: 2026-Oct-31
PMID: 42963954



Abstract:
Seychelles, the smallest country in Africa but with the highest GDP per capita, has experienced rapid socioeconomic development. We analysed 20-year cancer incidence trends (2005-2024) using data from the Seychelles National Cancer Registry (SNCR). Annual age-standardised incidence rates (ASRs), average annual percentage changes (AAPCs), and stage at diagnosis (for the four major cancers) were calculated. Incidence rates for the most recent decade (2015-2024) were also compared with those in selected African countries and high Human Development Index (HDI) countries. Among men, prostate cancer had the highest incidence (ASR 73.9 per 100,000) and increased significantly over time (AAPC +6.7%), reaching an ASR of 90.3 per 100,000 in 2015-2024. Significant declines were observed for oesophageal (AAPC -4.3%) and laryngeal cancers (AAPC -5.6%). Among women, breast cancer was the most common cancer (ASR 54.7 per 100,000), increasing by 3.4% annually and reaching an ASR of 70.5 per 100,000 in the most recent decade, comparable to rates in Europe. Significant increases were also observed for colorectal, cervical, and corpus uteri cancers. The observed trends reflect Seychelles' epidemiological transition, with a shift from infection-related cancers towards cancers associated with ageing and lifestyle factors, resembling the cancer profile of high-income countries. Nevertheless, the major cancers-prostate, breast, colorectal, and cervical-continue to be diagnosed at relatively advanced stages, highlighting the need for improved early detection and timely diagnosis.

item.title: Laser-Assisted Transoral Robotic Supraglottic Laryngectomy.
item.dc:creator: Tsur N, Costantino A, Magnuson JS
item.description:
Authors: Tsur N, Costantino A, Magnuson JS
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70516
Published: 2026-Oct-30
PMID: 42963910



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the operative setup, safety principles, and stepwise technique for laser-assisted transoral robotic supraglottic laryngectomy using a flexible CO2 laser system. METHODS: This operative video demonstrates laser-assisted transoral robotic supraglottic laryngectomy performed with the da Vinci SP platform. Key technical steps include laser-safe airway management, transoral exposure with a Feyh-Kastenbauer retractor, robotic docking, flexible CO2 laser fiber placement through a distal drop-in guide, aiming-beam confirmation, noncontact laser dissection, coordinated bedside suction and bipolar hemostasis, and en bloc specimen delivery. RESULTS: The technique allows controlled transoral access to the supraglottic larynx with three-dimensional visualization, precise noncontact laser incision, and preservation of uninvolved glottic and subglottic structures. A deliberate sequence of inferior, lateral, and superior release facilitates exposure of the pre-epiglottic space, specimen mobilization, and margin-oriented en bloc resection. CONCLUSION: Laser-assisted transoral robotic supraglottic laryngectomy combines the precision of CO2 laser surgery with the visualization and dexterity of single-port robotic surgery. With appropriate patient selection, strict laser safety, and a standardized team-based workflow, this technique can support precise en bloc resection, reliable margin assessment, and preservation of uninvolved laryngeal structures.

item.title: Geographical Location and Response to Trismus Rehabilitation Following Head and Neck Cancer Treatment: A Secondary Analysis of the Restorabite Trials.
item.dc:creator: Ricketts V, Charters E, Frowen J, Poke S, Gleeson S, Pryor L, Heng C, Adshead B, Lai M, Boehm J, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Ricketts V, Charters E, Frowen J, Poke S, Gleeson S, Pryor L, Heng C, Adshead B, Lai M, Boehm J, et al.
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70529
Published: 2026-Oct-30
PMID: 42963900



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trismus is a common and disabling complication following head and neck cancer (HNC) treatment, particularly after multimodal therapy. Survivors in regional areas face barriers to accessing specialist rehabilitation. This study explored whether a patient's geographical location of residence influenced their response to trismus therapy. METHODS: Secondary analysis of pooled data from three Restorabite trials (2021-2024) was performed. Adults with HNC-related trismus (maximal interincisal opening [MIO] ≤ 35 mm) completed a 10-week individualized rehabilitation program incorporating manual therapy, daily jaw exercises, and weekly speech pathology review delivered in person or via telehealth. Most participants (96.6%) received all or part of their intervention via telehealth. Outcomes included MIO and Gothenburg Trismus Questionnaire (GTQ) scores. Longitudinal change was modeled using generalized estimating equations. RESULTS: A total of 175 participants with a broad range of HNC subsites, tumor stage, and treatment modalities were included. MIO improved by an average of 1.2 mm/week and GTQ scores by -2.7 points/week after 10 weeks of trismus rehabilitation (both p < 0.001). While multimodal treatment had a negative effect on both MIO and GTQ, geographical residence was not associated with change in MIO or GTQ in adjusted models (p = 0.5 and p = 0.1, respectively). CONCLUSIONS: For geographically dispersed patients, geographical residence was not associated with poorer trismus outcomes within a predominantly telehealth-supported model of care, supporting the use of telehealth to facilitate access to specialist trismus rehabilitation.

item.title: Factors for Favorable Outcomes After Sialendoscopy for Radioactive Iodine-Induced Sialadenitis of Parotid Gland: An Exploratory Study Toward a Phenotypic Patterns.
item.dc:creator: Kim S, Park MJ, Kim JW
item.description:
Authors: Kim S, Park MJ, Kim JW
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70527
Published: 2026-Oct-30
PMID: 42963892



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radioactive iodine (RAI) therapy can induce radioactive iodine-induced sialadenitis (RAIS). Sialendoscopy is an effective treatment for RAIS, but predictors of favorable outcomes remain poorly defined. This study aimed to identify functional and anatomical factors associated with favorable outcomes following sialendoscopy in RAIS patients. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 44 cases who underwent sialendoscopy for RAIS. Favorable outcome was defined as a symptom resolution without the need for additional medication or revision surgery. RESULTS: In the multivariate model, ΔSFR(pre) (difference between stimulated and unstimulated preoperative SFR) (p = 0.035), symptom duration (p = 0.039), and distal stenosis (p = 0.024) were confirmed as predictors. ROC curve analysis determined the optimal cutoffs for the two continuous independent predictors: low ΔSFR(pre) < 0.41, early intervention < 4.5 months. CONCLUSIONS: This study identified low ΔSFR(pre), early intervention, and distal stenosis of Stenson's duct as associated with favorable outcome.

item.title: Comparison of HPV Antibodies Measured Prior to Diagnosis of Anal, Cervical, Oropharyngeal, Penile and Vaginal Cancers in the HPV Cancer Cohort Consortium.
item.dc:creator: Onwuka JU, Nobels MP, Kreimer AR, Schroeder L, Ferreiro-Iglesias A, Agalliu I, Albanes D, Cai Q, D'Souza G, Freedman ND, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Onwuka JU, Nobels MP, Kreimer AR, Schroeder L, Ferreiro-Iglesias A, Agalliu I, Albanes D, Cai Q, D'Souza G, Freedman ND, et al.
Journal: International journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1002/ijc.70786
Published: 2026-Oct-30
PMID: 42963861



Abstract:
Antibodies against HPV proteins can provide pre-diagnostic information about cancer development. We described the prevalence of antibodies to proteins of oncogenic HPV types prior to diagnosis of HPV-related cancers. We analysed pre-diagnostic blood from 1700 participants with incident HPV-related cancers (anal = 387, cervical = 274, oropharyngeal = 788, penile = 168, vaginal = 83) and 6221 controls from nine prospective cohorts in Europe, North America and Australia in the HPV Cancer Cohort Consortium. We measured antibodies against E6, E7 and L1 proteins for 6 HPV types, and additionally against E1, E2, E4, E6, E7 and L1 proteins of HPV16 and 18. We described seroprevalence by lead time from blood draw to cancer diagnosis (range: 0-43 years). We found that among oropharyngeal cancers, seroprevalence increased approaching diagnosis for HPV16 E1, E2, E4, E6, E7, L1 and HPV18 E1, E2, L1 (HPV16-E6: from 10.4% at > 20 years to 35.8% at 0-5 years, vs. 0.3% in controls). Anal cancer showed similar patterns for HPV16 E1, E2, E4, E6 and L1 and HPV18 E2 (HPV16-E6: from 3.8% at > 20 years to 29.8% at 0-5 years). No trends were observed for cervical, penile, or vaginal cancers. In a multivariable model fit among cases, HPV16-E6 seropositivity was higher at shorter lead times and more recent calendar periods, lower among US non-Hispanic Blacks, and varied by cancer type (highest in oropharyngeal followed by anal, vaginal, penile and cervical) (all p < 0.03). In conclusion, pre-diagnostic HPV antibody responses vary by cancer type, with seroprevalence of 6-9 HPV proteins increasing approaching diagnosis for oropharyngeal and anal cancers, but not cervical, penile or vaginal cancers.

item.title: Pediatric Recurrent Croup: An International Delphi Consensus Statement.
item.dc:creator: Crotty TJ, Cleere EF, Alhyari F, McBride A, Schaefer S, Heffernan CB
item.description:
Authors: Crotty TJ, Cleere EF, Alhyari F, McBride A, Schaefer S, Heffernan CB
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71022
Published: 2026-Oct-30
PMID: 42963314



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Recurrent croup lacks a consistent diagnostic definition, resulting in substantial variation in investigation and management. We aimed to develop international consensus-based recommendations for the evaluation and management of pediatric recurrent croup. DATA SOURCES: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and EMBASE searched from 1st January 2000 to 15th August 2026, with results reported in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. REVIEW METHODS: An international modified Delphi consensus process was conducted. Panelists rated statements using a 9-point Likert scale across two rounds. Strong consensus was defined as a mean ≥ 8.00 with no outliers; consensus as mean ≥ 7.00 with no more than one outlier. RESULTS: Review of 28 studies confirmed substantial heterogeneity in the definition and investigation of recurrent croup, with most studies at moderate to high risk of bias. Strong consensus was achieved on prioritizing direct laryngoscopy and bronchoscopy in atypical presentations, including subglottic sizing and exclusion of a laryngeal cleft, and limiting allergy testing to children with clinical suspicion of atopic disease. Consensus supported shared otolaryngology-respiratory management, avoidance of routine imaging, and reserving advanced reflux investigation for refractory cases. No consensus was reached on empirical inhaled corticosteroids or antireflux therapy. CONCLUSION: This study provides the first international multidisciplinary consensus guidance for the evaluation and management of recurrent croup, supported by a proposed risk-stratified management algorithm. Agreement on core diagnostic and endoscopic priorities may help standardize clinical practice, while the absence of consensus on optimal medical management identifies clear priorities for future research in a field where high-quality prospective data remain lacking. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: N/A.

item.title: DNA Immunotherapy (INO-3107) Long-Term Efficacy Supported by Enhanced Immunogenicity in HPV-6/11 RRP.
item.dc:creator: Amin MR, Belafsky PC, Best SR, Friedman AD, Klein AM, Lott DG, Mau T, Paniello RC, Pransky SM, Saba NF, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Amin MR, Belafsky PC, Best SR, Friedman AD, Klein AM, Lott DG, Mau T, Paniello RC, Pransky SM, Saba NF, et al.
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71016
Published: 2026-Oct-30
PMID: 42963203



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP), caused by chronic HPV-6/11 infection, leads to repeated papilloma growth requiring frequent surgical removal. DNA immunotherapy INO-3107 aims to induce HPV antigen-specific T-cell responses and reduce surgical burden. This analysis evaluated HPV-specific immune responses after INO-3107 and their association with long-term clinical outcomes. METHODS: Adults with HPV-6/11-associated RRP received INO-3107 in a Phase 1/2 trial and were followed for one year, with additional clinical follow-up in a long-term extension. Number of surgeries in Years 1 and 2 was compared with the pre-treatment year. Blood and laryngotracheal tissue collected at Day 0 and Year 1 were analyzed for treatment-related changes in T-cell activity. Safety was assessed throughout. RESULTS: Thirty-two patients were treated; 28 continued into Year 2. At Year 1, most evaluable patients showed increased T-cell activity: 73% (19/26) demonstrated persistent expanded T-cell populations in blood, 71% (12/17) showed higher T-cell clone counts in laryngotracheal tissue, indicating site-specific immune infiltration. Antiviral T-cell signatures were enriched in 88% for CD4+ Th1 and CD8+ cytotoxic, and 71% for CD8+ effector memory, suggesting durable proinflammatory and memory responses in airway tissue. Mean annual surgeries decreased over time in the overall population (Baseline: 4.1, Year 1: 1.7, Year 2: 0.9). Similar durable reductions were observed in Responder subgroups. INO-3107 was well-tolerated, with no treatment-related serious adverse events. CONCLUSION: INO-3107 generates increased HPV-directed T-cell responses and substantially reduced surgical procedures over two years, supporting its ability to provide long-term clinical benefit in RRP without requiring additional surgeries during the dosing window.

item.title: Efficacy and safety of oral orforglipron in Japanese participants with obesity disease (ATTAIN-J): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 trial.
item.dc:creator: Yokote K, Yamauchi T, Shingaki T, Chin R, Oura T, Nagai Y, Shimomura I, Kadowaki T
item.description:
Authors: Yokote K, Yamauchi T, Shingaki T, Chin R, Oura T, Nagai Y, Shimomura I, Kadowaki T
Journal: The lancet. Diabetes & endocrinology | DOI: 10.1016/S2213-8587(26)00232-9
Published: 2026-Oct-30
PMID: 42962687



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Orforglipron, a small-molecule, non-peptide, oral GLP-1 receptor agonist, has shown bodyweight reduction and cardiometabolic benefits in adults with obesity across phase 3 trials globally. We aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of orforglipron versus placebo for treating obesity disease in Japanese adults. METHODS: ATTAIN-J was a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 trial conducted across 16 medical research centres and hospitals in Japan and included adults aged 18 years or older with a BMI between 27 kg/m2 and less than 35 kg/m2 and two or more obesity-related health disorders, or a BMI of 35 kg/m2 or higher and one or more obesity-related health disorder, with one or more of the obesity-related health disorders being hypertension, dyslipidaemia, or type 2 diabetes (targeted at about 25% of participants), consistent with Japanese indications for tirzepatide and semaglutide for obesity disease; and at least one unsuccessful dietary attempt to lose weight. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) via a computer-generated sequence to once-daily oral orforglipron (6 mg, 12 mg, or 36 mg) or placebo. Co-primary endpoints were mean percentage change in bodyweight and percentage of participants with at least 5% bodyweight reduction from baseline to week 72. Efficacy endpoints were primarily evaluated by the treatment regimen estimand in all randomly assigned participants. Safety was assessed in participants who received at least one dose of study treatment. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05931380 (completed). FINDINGS: Between July 31, 2023, and June 19, 2025, 291 participants were screened, of whom 238 (144 [61%] males and 94 [39%] females; mean age 54·1 years [SD 11·2]) were randomly assigned to receive orforglipron 6 mg (n=61), 12 mg (n=57), or 36 mg (n=60), or placebo (n=60); 214 (90%) participants completed the study. At week 72, mean percentage change in bodyweight was -5·9% (95% CI -7·6 to -4·2) with orforglipron 6 mg, -8·7% (-10·9 to -6·5) with 12 mg, and -7·9% (-10·0 to -5·8) with 36 mg, compared with -0·6% (-2·1 to 0·8) with placebo (all p<0·0001 vs placebo). At week 72, a bodyweight reduction of at least 5% was seen in 15·2% (SE 4·8; nine of 60) of participants in the placebo group compared with 45·6% (6·1; 28 of 61; p=0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 6 mg group, 60·8% (6·4; 35 of 57; p<0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 12 mg group, and 58·8% (6·5; 35 of 60; p<0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 36 mg group. Adverse events with orforglipron were mostly mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal symptoms. Across all orforglipron groups, treatment-emergent adverse events that most frequently led to study treatment discontinuation were nausea (one [2%] of 61 in the 6 mg group, one [2%] of 57 in the 12 mg group, and five [8%] of 60 in the 36 mg group vs none with placebo) and vomiting (none in the 6 mg group, two [4%] in the 12 mg group, and one [2%] in the 36 mg group vs none in the placebo group). INTERPRETATION: In Japanese adults with obesity disease, once-daily orforglipron resulted in statistically superior reductions in bodyweight versus placebo, with a safety profile consistent with that of other GLP-1 receptor agonists. FUNDING: Eli Lilly and Company. TRANSLATION: For the Japanese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

item.title: Efficacy of immediate radiotherapy versus salvage radiotherapy in patients with de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma responsive to chemoimmunotherapy.
item.dc:creator: Zhang QT, He JR, Guo HB, Sun YN, Chen J, Cheng H, Xiao YX, Sun XS, Wu LF, Li XY, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Zhang QT, He JR, Guo HB, Sun YN, Chen J, Cheng H, Xiao YX, Sun XS, Wu LF, Li XY, et al.
Journal: ESMO open | DOI: 10.1016/j.esmoop.2026.108608
Published: 2026-Oct-30
PMID: 42962562



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chemoimmunotherapy has become the standard first-line treatment for de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (dmNPC). However, the role and optimal timing of locoregional radiotherapy in dmNPC in the chemoimmunotherapy era remain unclear. This study aims to evaluate whether salvage locoregional radiotherapy (SLRRT), deferred until locoregional progression in patients with well-controlled distant metastases, compromises survival compared with immediate locoregional radiotherapy (ILRRT) in responders to first-line chemoimmunotherapy. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with dmNPC who achieved a complete or partial response after first-line platinum-based chemotherapy combined with anti-programmed cell death protein 1 therapy. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS). Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was applied to adjust for baseline characteristics. Survival outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analyses and a multivariate Cox regression model. RESULTS: A total of 439 patients were included, with a median follow-up of 35.0 months (interquartile range, 24.0-45.2). Of these, 331 patients were assigned to the ILRRT cohort and 108 to the SLRRT cohort. After IPTW adjustment, SLRRT was not associated with inferior OS compared with ILRRT [2-year OS, 97.4% versus 90.1%; hazard ratio (HR) 0.93, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.54-1.59, P = 0.78]. CONCLUSIONS: Deferring SLRRT until locoregional progression did not compromise survival among responders to first-line chemoimmunotherapy. item.title: Mechanism study on CSF3-Induced M2 polarization of tumor-associated macrophages and CCL9 secretion in promoting tumor progression in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.

item.description:
Authors: Xie Y, Lin Y, He J, Ji Y, Luo X, An W, Sun Y, Qiao X, Li Z
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108176
Published: 2026-Oct-30

Abstract:
Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) accounts for ∼85% of head and neck cancers and is the sixth most common malignancy worldwide. Standard surgery plus chemoradiotherapy has limited success due to high recurrence. Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) in the tumor microenvironment (TME) promote tumor growth, invasion and angiogenesis. Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor 3 (CSF3) regulates neutrophil function and may influence monocyte differentiation into M2 macrophages in breast and bladder cancers. This study aims to investigate CSF3's role in promoting TAM-M2 polarization in HNSCC and explore the mechanisms using in vitro and in vivo approaches. Bioinformatic methods analyzed CSF3's clinicopathological significance and association with M2 infiltration. CSF3 expression was evaluated in paired tumor/normal tissues by RT-qPCR and IHC, and serum levels by ELISA. CSF3-modulated cell lines were co-cultured with TAMs; polarization was assessed via marker expression by RT-qPCR and flow cytometry. CSF3-overexpressing mouse models examined tumor growth and CD206 expression by IHC. Functional assays on MOC2 cells used TAM-conditioned supernatant. RNA-seq and CCL9 secretion were analyzed. CSF3 correlated with poor prognosis and increased M2 infiltration. Elevated CSF3 mRNA/protein were detected in tumor tissues and serum. CSF3 overexpression promoted M2 polarization, CD206 expression, and tumor growth. Conditioned medium from TAMs co-cultured with CSF3-knockdown tumor cells attenuated MOC2 proliferation, migration and invasion. Tumor-derived CSF3 upregulated TAM-derived CCL9, and exogenous CCL9 restored pro-tumor effects. Elevated CSF3 in HNSCC promotes TAM-M2 polarization and induces CCL9 production in polarized TAMs, creating a pro-tumor microenvironment that facilitates HNSCC progression.

item.title: Age-specific income losses due to HPV-attributable cancers in Singapore.
item.dc:creator: Blythe R, Graves N, Iyer NG, Peres MA
item.description:
Authors: Blythe R, Graves N, Iyer NG, Peres MA
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361921
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42961926



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The link between Human Papillomavirus (HPV) and cancer is well-established. In Singapore, bivalent HPV vaccines are subsidised for females, but not males. Economic analysis of HPV vaccination has generally assessed the costs to the health system, but this may not be as relevant to individual decision-making as potential lost income. We estimated the impact of bivalent HPV 16/18 vaccination on sick leave, unemployment, and premature mortality as a function of age and sex to understand the broader impact of HPV-related cancers. METHODS: We developed a population-level economic model to estimate lifetime income losses by diagnosis age, sex and cancer type. We applied sex- and cancer-specific Cox regressions to the Singapore Cancer Registry for annual predicted survival from 1992 to 2022. These were combined with census and employment data to estimate HPV-associated income losses in Singapore. Attributable fractions and vaccine effectiveness data for HPV 16/18 from the literature were used to estimate the effectiveness of bivalent HPV vaccination. Structural sensitivity analysis examined the role of 80% population coverage conferring herd immunity. RESULTS: The registry contained 17,294 individuals with an HPV-associated cancer diagnosis. Lost income was greatest for cervical cancer due to its high prevalence, however the losses per diagnosis were highest for oropharyngeal cancer. Bivalent HPV vaccination led to income benefits of $SGD1,397 [$895 to $1,838] in girls and -$62 [-$76 to -$48] in boys. A gender-neutral HPV vaccination of 80% of 15-year-old Singaporeans, conferring herd immunity, would have lifetime income protective benefits of $24.4m [$14.2m, $33.7m] per cohort, a five-fold return on investment. CONCLUSIONS: In addition to avoiding healthcare costs and lost quality of life, parents should consider vaccination as a means of avoiding potential income losses. A national policy of gender-neutral HPV vaccination could deliver substantial income protection due to both individual vaccine protection and herd immunity.

item.title: Edentulism and functional disability in older adults: A longitudinal and cross-national study in England, the United States, and India.
item.dc:creator: Tang W, He L, Zhang M, Li J
item.description:
Authors: Tang W, He L, Zhang M, Li J
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361422
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42961862



Abstract:
Edentulism may contribute to functional disability in older adults, yet cross-national evidence combining multiple analytic strategies and mechanistic assessment remains limited. This study examined the association between edentulism and disability in activities of daily living (ADL) and instrumental activities of daily living (IADL) across England, the United States, and India. We analyzed harmonized data from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA; n = 9,102), the Health and Retirement Study (HRS; n = 22,156), and the Longitudinal Ageing Study in India (LASI; n = 31,816) for adults aged 60 years or older. Cross-sectional associations were estimated using inverse probability weighting (IPW) and augmented IPW. Longitudinal Cox proportional hazards models were applied in ELSA and HRS. Mediation through grip strength, body mass index (BMI), and depressive symptoms was assessed with counterfactual causal mediation analysis on the risk-difference scale. Edentulism was associated with higher odds of ADL (pooled odds ratio 1.30, 95% confidence interval 1.20-1.42) and IADL disability (1.27, 1.11-1.45). Longitudinal analyses confirmed elevated hazard ratios for incident ADL (1.19, 1.09-1.30) and IADL disability (1.30, 1.19-1.43). Grip strength accounted for the largest proportion mediated (approximately 50% in ELSA and HRS, and 5-14% in LASI); BMI and depressive symptoms showed little mediation. In LASI, denture use among edentulous participants was associated with lower disability odds. Edentulism was consistently associated with functional disability across three countries, with grip strength partially accounting for this association, although the cross-sectional design precludes establishing temporality. Oral rehabilitation may partly buffer this risk and merits further prospective investigation.

item.title: Academic Attributes and Institutional Characteristics of U.S. Otolaryngology-Head & Neck Surgery Residency Program Directors.

Authors: Reddy PD, Aguilar B, Tang AJ, Harris M, Whelan R, Maxwell JH, Jabbour N
Journal: The Annals of otology, rhinology, and laryngology | DOI: 10.1177/00034894261501326
Published: 2026-Oct-30

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the academic attributes and appointment patterns of current U.S. Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery residency program directors (PDs). STUDY DESIGN: Cross-sectional analysis accredited Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery residency programs in the United States. METHODS: One hundred and twenty six U.S. otolaryngology program directors were analyzed. Descriptive data, including academic productivity (publications, H-index), gender, NIH funding, and subspecialties, were collected from publicly available sources. RESULTS: We found that 63.5% (80/126) of PDs are male, and nearly half (49.2%; 62/126) completed some training at their current institution, while most were later promoted internally after joining the faculty. Advanced degrees (PhD, MBA, MPH) were held by 18.3% (23/126) and were associated with nearly double the publication output (80.0 vs 40.8 publications; P < .01). External hires accounted for 8.3% (10/120) and trended toward higher H-index values (17.4 vs 12.0, P = .25), total publications (94.9 vs 45.4, P = .226), and NIH funding rates (10.0% vs 2.7%, P = .30) than internal hires. The most common subspecialties were Head & Neck Surgery (20.6%; 26/126) and Rhinology (18.3%; 23/126). CONCLUSION: Otolaryngology PDs are often internal hires, with nearly half completing some portion of their training at their current institution. A significant portion of PDs hold additional advanced degrees, which are associated with increased academic productivity. For those considering a career in educational leadership, understanding prevailing academic backgrounds and institutional hiring patterns may help inform career planning.

Authors: Paris J, Tsimiklis J, Agarwal A, Tong JY, Selva D
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70533
Published: 2026-Oct-29

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immunotherapy is increasingly used for head and neck cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) with perineural spread (PNS), though outcomes remain poorly defined. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA and MOOSE guidelines. Studies reporting immunotherapy in cSCC with clinical or radiologic cranial nerve PNS were included. Data on demographics, nerve involvement, treatment, response, and outcomes were extracted. RESULTS: Twenty-three studies (150 patients) were included. Median age was 72.5 years; 78.5% were male. PNS most commonly involved CNV (83.3%) and CNVII (31.7%). Immunotherapy was primarily cemiplimab (75.2%) and pembrolizumab (19.7%). Disease control was achieved in 87.3% (complete response: 38.7%, partial response: 42.0%). Functional nerve recovery was reported in 26/64 patients with evaluable outcomes (40.6%), equivalent to 17.3% of the total cohort. Median follow-up was 16 months, with 82.3% alive. Adverse events occurred in 28%, with serious toxicity rare. CONCLUSIONS: The available evidence demonstrates that immunotherapy can achieve disease control in cSCC with PNS and that established cranial nerve dysfunction may recover in some patients. Prospective studies with standardized oncological and functional outcomes are needed to better define treatment efficacy and establish the role of immunotherapy within current treatment paradigms.

item.title: A clinical multimodal vision language foundation model with fine-grain explainability.
item.dc:creator: Bai Y, Cheng H, Zhou Y, Zhou J, Thirunavukarasu A, Ke Y, Yao J, Fukutsu K, Quek CWN, Hong ASY, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Bai Y, Cheng H, Zhou Y, Zhou J, Thirunavukarasu A, Ke Y, Yao J, Fukutsu K, Quek CWN, Hong ASY, et al.
Journal: Nature medicine | DOI: 10.1038/s41591-026-04655-5
Published: 2026-Oct-29

Abstract:
Despite their considerable promise, many current medical foundation models remain modality specific and lack transparent reasoning, limiting clinical adoption. To address this gap, we introduce Explainable Vision Language Foundation Model for Medicine (EVLF-FM), a multimodal vision language foundation model that combines broad diagnostic capabilities with fine-grained explainability. The development and testing of EVLF-FM encompassed more than 1.3 million total samples from 18 global datasets across 10 imaging modalities related to six clinical specialties: dermatology, hepatology, ophthalmology, pathology, pulmonology and radiology. External validation employed 13,443 independent test samples from 17 additional datasets across 10 imaging modalities. EVLF-FM supports disease diagnosis, visual question answering and pixel-level visual grounding with reasoning capabilities. In internal validation for disease diagnostics, EVLF-FM achieved the highest average accuracy, 0.895, outperforming leading generalist and specialist models. In medical visual grounding, EVLF-FM also achieved reasonable performance across nine modalities with average accuracy at 0.5 intersection over union (Acc@0.5) of 0.842. External testing further confirmed consistent zero-shot and few-shot performance, with competitive F1 scores despite a smaller model size. A hybrid training strategy combining supervised and visual reinforcement fine-tuning enables EVLF-FM to generate clinically interpretable explanations aligned with visual evidence. Human evaluation of these reasoning outputs using the S.C.O.R.E. framework yielded a high overall mean score of 4.25/5, supporting their clinical interpretability. Current limitations include the need for additional validation across diverse healthcare settings. Prospective clinical studies are required to evaluate the safety, effectiveness and clinical utility of EVLF-FM before routine clinical deployment.

item.title: IL-36γ/IL-36R axis reprograms cancer-associated fibroblasts to promote OSCC invasion via ERK1/2-CCL20-mediated ECM remodeling.
item.dc:creator: Li Z, Zhang Y, Luo W, Jing Y, Yu Q, Song Y, Lu W, Xia S, Chen X, Yu H, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Li Z, Zhang Y, Luo W, Jing Y, Yu Q, Song Y, Lu W, Xia S, Chen X, Yu H, et al.
Journal: Oncogene | DOI: 10.1038/s41388-026-04030-1

Abstract:
The IL-36γ/IL-36R signaling axis mediates cellular communication in various contexts and has recently been implicated in pro-fibrotic responses. However, its specific role in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), which is characterized by abundant cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), remains elusive. Here, we investigated the contribution of IL-36γ/IL-36R signaling to CAF function and OSCC progression. Immunohistochemical analysis of patient samples revealed that IL-36γ was highly expressed in CAFs and that higher co-expression of IL-36γ/IL-36R in CAFs was associated with more invasive patterns and shorter disease-free survival. These models revealed that IL-36γ signaling enhanced CAF proliferation and extracellular matrix remodeling. Collectively, these findings suggest that the IL-36γ/IL-36R-ERK1/2-CCL20 signaling cascade participates in CAF-tumor interactions. Targeting IL-36R may therefore represent a promising therapeutic strategy for invasive OSCC.

Abstract:
We examine the material and conceptual impact of the Coalition for the Reproductive Rights of Workers (CRROW) during the late 1970s. item.title: Improved model predictive current control strategy for overvoltage suppression in long-cable PWM-driven induction motor electrical submersible pump systems.
item.dc:creator: Gong X, Qi X, Feng M, Zhu L, Wang N
item.description:
Authors: Gong X, Qi X, Feng M, Zhu L, Wang N
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360296
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42956049



Abstract:
Long-cable PWM-driven induction motor electric submersible pump (ESP) systems suffer from significant voltage reflection issues caused by distributed parameter effects, leading to transient overvoltages at the motor terminals that can reach several times the DC bus voltage. This severely threatens system stability and motor insulation integrity, and traditional control methods prove inadequate for effective suppression. To address this challenge, the paper proposes an improved model predictive current control (MPCC) strategy for induction motor ESP systems, which integrates overvoltage suppression and equivalent switching frequency reduction for long-cable PWM-driven applications. The reflection overvoltage mechanism is thoroughly analyzed through mathematical modeling of the motor and long-cable transmission line, and the applicability of predictive current control in such systems is investigated. The core improvement lies in a circular boundary constrained MPCC combined with a dynamic transition voltage vector selection mechanism, which enables dual-mode optimization based on current error boundary conditions: the normal cost function is applied within the circular boundary to jointly optimize voltage tracking, switching frequency, and dv/dt; while the backup cost function is activated outside the boundary to prioritize current error minimization. This effectively optimizes the voltage switching strategy, reducing both switching frequency and dv/dt, thereby preventing overvoltage excitation caused by abrupt voltage vector steps in PWM-driven systems. Simulation models under different cable configurations (1 km with RLC filter and 110 m without RLC filter) and an experimental platform based on a neutral-point-clamped three-level inverter (NPC-TLI) topology are established, with the 110 m no-filter configuration serving as a direct cross-validation baseline. Comparative simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed strategy significantly reduces the duration of motor terminal overvoltage while maintaining excellent system dynamic performance. Moreover, the improved MPCC effectively suppresses overvoltage and reduces equivalent switching frequency without requiring hardware filter redesign, while the RLC filter remains necessary for full insulation safety compliance under more demanding long-cable conditions, substantially mitigating the risk of motor insulation breakdown.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Achieving early glycemic control in adolescents with diabetes is associated with improved short- and long-term health outcomes. RESULTS: The mean age of the participants was 14 ± 2.3 years and 49.7% had diabetes between 1-5 years. The mean total score of the EAT scale was 16.62 ± 8.30. item.title: Identification of prognostic biomarkers for nasopharyngeal carcinoma through microRNA‑mRNA network analysis combined with screening of immune‑related genes.

item.description:
Authors: He L, Huang X, Huang P
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361607
Published: 2026-01-01

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a common head and neck cancer, and radiotherapy is its main treatment. Recurrence and metastasis are the main causes of treatment failure. Although immunotherapy can prolong patient survival, the molecular mechanisms underlying NPC development and progression remain unclear. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) and their target genes are abnormally expressed in many tumors and are closely involved in tumor development. The core genes were further overlapped with immune-related gene sets, followed by functional enrichment analysis. A prognostic risk model was established using LASSO-Cox regression, and immune cell infiltration was evaluated with CIBERSORT. Model validation, immunohistochemical analysis, and drug-gene interaction analysis were also performed. In vitro, RT-qPCR was conducted in C666-1 and NP69 cell lines to verify the expression of key genes. RESULTS: We identified 213 potential target genes of key miRNAs. item.title: Patient Experiences With ctHPVDNA-Guided Surveillance for HPV-Positive Oropharyngeal Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Fleming GE, Roth H, Hanna GJ, Sethi RKV, Minken J, Mukundan D, Schoenfeld JD, Windon MJ, Rettig EM
item.description:
Authors: Fleming GE, Roth H, Hanna GJ, Sethi RKV, Minken J, Mukundan D, Schoenfeld JD, Windon MJ, Rettig EM

Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Circulating tumor human papillomavirus DNA (ctHPVDNA) is a potential biomarker for surveillance of HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer. Despite its growing clinical use, patient experiences are not well characterized, and understanding patient perspectives of ctHPVDNA-guided surveillance is essential to guiding its appropriate use while mitigating potential harms. OBJECTIVE: To characterize patient experiences with ctHPVDNA-guided surveillance. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: A mixed-methods cross-sectional interview study in adults treated for HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer with 1 or more surveillance ctHPVDNA test 3 or more months before enrollment conducted in June through August 2025 in a single tertiary academic cancer center. Purposive sampling ensured representation of diverse patient experiences. EXPOSURES: One semistructured interview regarding experiences with ctHPVDNA-guided surveillance. Willingness to pay (WTP) out of pocket was assessed using iterative bidding. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Themes and subthemes were derived from coded interview transcripts using a categorical inductive approach. RESULTS: Among 20 participants (median age, 58 years [IQR, 55-70 years]; 16 males [80%]), 8 (40%) had true-negative ctHPVDNA test results, 6 had true-positive results (30%), 4 had false-negative results (20%), and 2 had false-positive results (10%). The median per-test WTP was $325 (range, $0-$9000). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This study found that participants expressed strong support for ctHPVDNA-guided surveillance. Trust in clinicians appeared to mitigate distress related to confusing or inaccurate test results. Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Head and neck osteosarcomas (HNOS) are rare, accounting for ~1% of head and neck malignancies. This study systematically evaluated the role of chemotherapy (CT) and radiotherapy (RT) on survival outcomes. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were performed following PRISMA guidelines across six databases. Abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare prophylactic (p-) versus reactive (r-) percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) placement during definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT) for locally advanced, nonmetastatic head and neck carcinoma, with swallowing-related quality of life (QoL) as the primary endpoint. MATERIALS AND METHODS: SwallPEG is a prospective, multicenter, randomized phase III trial of patients undergoing definitive cisplatin-based CRT. Patients were randomized 1:1 to pPEG before CRT or rPEG based on predefined nutritional criteria. All received standardized nutritional counseling, weekly dietitian assessment, and swallowing rehabilitation. The primary endpoint was swallowing-related QoL at 6 months, assessed using the MD Anderson Dysphagia Inventory (MDADI) composite score. Secondary endpoints included nutritional outcomes, treatment-related toxicity, PEG-related complications, and early oncologic outcomes. RESULTS: Fifty-seven patients were analyzed (pPEG, n = 28; rPEG, n = 29). Following a prespecified interim analysis that reached the futility boundary, the trial was closed early in the context of slow accrual. Median MDADI composite scores at 6 months were 69.5 (Q1-Q3, 60.0-80.0) and 74.7 (Q1-Q3, 58.9-87.9), respectively (P = 0.595). CONCLUSION: No difference in swallowing-related QoL was demonstrated between (p-) and rPEG strategies. Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination at the earliest opportunity is critical for preventing cervical, vulvar, vaginal, anal, rectal, and oropharyngeal cancers. METHODS: We analyzed Iowa Immunization Registry Information System data for youth aged 9-17 years, linked to ZIP Code Tabulation Area socioeconomic and demographic measures. item.title: Talazoparib plus enzalutamide versus placebo plus enzalutamide in metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant (castration-resistant) prostate cancer (TALAPRO-2): a biomarker analysis of circulating tumour DNA and cells for prognosis and molecular profiling.

item.description:

Journal: The Lancet. Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/S1470-2045(26)00355-4
Published: 2026-Oct-28

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The TALAPRO-2 trial showed improved radiographic progression-free survival and overall survival with first-line talazoparib plus enzalutamide versus placebo plus enzalutamide in patients with metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant prostate cancer (APMR; also referred to as castration-resistant prostate cancer) unselected for homologous recombination repair (HRR) gene alterations treated. We aimed to assess HRR gene alteration status agreement between prospective solid tumour tissue and circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) testing, the potential complementary value of prospective and retrospective ctDNA testing, and the prognostic utility of baseline ctDNA burden, changes in ctDNA burden, and circulating tumour cell (CTC) reductions. METHODS: In TALAPRO-2, a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial, men aged 18 years or older (≥20 years in Japan) with asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic metastatic APMR prostate cancer and no previous life-prolonging systemic therapy for APMR disease were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive once daily, oral talazoparib 0·5 mg plus enzalutamide 160 mg or placebo plus enzalutamide and stratified by HRR gene alteration status and previous treatment for androgen pathway modulator-naive/sensitive disease. The sponsor, patients, and investigators were masked to allocation of talazoparib or placebo; enzalutamide was open label. In this exploratory analysis, HRR gene alteration status agreement was evaluated in the unselected intention-to-treat cohort between solid tumour tissue prospectively tested using a clinical trial assay based on FoundationOne CDx and retrospectively tested ctDNA samples, collected at screening and assessed using an assay based on FoundationOne Liquid CDx. Tumour burden was categorised as positive or negative (ctDNA tumour fraction detectable or not detectable). Reductions in CTCs, enumerated using CELLSEARCH, were defined as conversion (from five or more cells per 7·5 mL of blood to four or fewer cells per 7·5 mL of blood) or CTC0 (from one or more cells per 7·5 mL of blood to zero). Radiographic progression-free survival was assessed for patients with baseline ctDNA positivity (positive vs negative) and for patients with ctDNA conversion and CTC conversion and CTC0 at week 9 (and week 17 for CTC conversion and CTC0) by treatment group. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrial.gov, NCT03395197 and is active, not recruiting. FINDINGS: Between Jan 7, 2019, and Sept 17, 2020, 805 patients were enrolled and randomly assigned (402 to talazoparib plus enzalutamide; 403 to placebo plus enzalutamide); median follow-up for radiographic progression-free survival was 24·9 months (IQR 21·9-30·2) for the talazoparib group and 24·6 months (14·4-30·2) for the placebo group. A high concordance in HRR gene alteration status was observed between results from prospectively tested solid tumour tissue samples and retrospectively tested screening ctDNA samples (reported for 739 [92%] of 805 enrolled patients), with 84% (421 of 501) agreement in patients evaluable as either HRR-deficient or HRR-non-deficient by both tests. Median radiographic progression-free survival for positive versus negative ctDNA burden was 21·0 months (95% CI 16·5-not reached [NR]) versus NR (NR-NR), respectively (hazard ratio [HR] 2·46; 95% CI 1·68-3·60; p<0·0001) with talazoparib plus enzalutamide, and 11·0 months (8·4-13·8) versus 33·2 months (30·3-NR), respectively (HR 4·03; 2·85-5·72; p<0·0001) with placebo plus enzalutamide. Patients remaining ctDNA negative had more favourable radiographic progression-free survival versus conversion from positive to negative ctDNA. CTC conversion and CTC0 at week 9 were prognostic for radiographic progression-free survival benefit in both groups. INTERPRETATION: Our results support broad prognostic utility of ctDNA burden and CTC enumeration in metastatic APMR prostate cancer, including in the context of poly(ADP) ribose polymerase inhibitor therapy. item.title: Darovasertib and Crizotinib First-Line Treatment for Metastatic Uveal Melanoma: Overall Survival, Efficacy, and Safety From the OptimUM-01 Study.
item.dc:creator: McKean M, Chmielowski B, Butler MO, Carvajal RD, Rodon J, Carlino MS, Kim KB, Wise-Draper TM, Khan S, Salama AKS, et al.
item.description:
Authors: McKean M, Chmielowski B, Butler MO, Carvajal RD, Rodon J, Carlino MS, Kim KB, Wise-Draper TM, Khan S, Salama AKS, et al.
Journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology | DOI: 10.1200/JCO-26-00802
Published: 2026-Oct-28
PMID: 42950186



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Metastatic uveal melanoma (mUM) has poor prognosis with limited therapies. GNAQ/11 mutations that activate protein kinase C (PKC) are detected in 95% of UM tumors. Darovasertib is a first-in-class, oral, targeted PKC inhibitor that, in combination with the MET inhibitor crizotinib, has shown responses and encouraging survival outcomes in early mUM clinical trials. Here, we present phase 2 results in first-line patients with mUM treated with darovasertib 300 mg twice a day and crizotinib 200 mg twice a day. METHODS: The OptimUM-01 study was a phase I/II, multicenter, open-label, dose escalation and expansion study of darovasertib in patients with solid tumors harboring GNAQ/11 mutations irrespective of human leukocyte antigen status; this analysis focuses on the phase II expansion in previously untreated patients with mUM. Eligibility criteria included Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors v1.1 measurable disease, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0-1, and adequate organ function. Study end points included safety, objective response rate (ORR), duration of response (DOR), disease control rate (DCR), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS). RESULTS: Overall, 44 treatment-naïve patients were enrolled. The most common adverse events (AEs) were diarrhea (95.2%), nausea (84.1%), peripheral edema (61.4%), and vomiting (52.3%). The most common grade 3 or greater AEs were pulmonary embolism (9.1%) and iron deficiency anemia (6.8%). AEs leading to discontinuation occurred in three patients (6.8%). ORR was 34.1%, DOR was 9.0 months, and DCR was 90.2% at 8 weeks. The median PFS and OS were 7.0 months (95% CI, 5.0 to 8.3) and 21.1 months (95% CI, 11.9 to 20.7), respectively. CONCLUSION: Results from OptimUM-01 suggest that the combination of darovasertib and crizotinib has encouraging efficacy with a manageable safety profile and may represent a first-in-class targeted treatment option for patients with previously untreated mUM.

item.title: Multimedia versus audio-based education for improving dentists' nutrition-related knowledge and behavior: A randomized comparative study.

Authors: Farhadi M, Pakdaman A, Gholami M
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360426
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42949884



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nutrition plays a crucial role in oral health, influencing the risk of caries, periodontal disease, erosion, and oral cancers. Dentists are key providers of dietary guidance, but require adequate knowledge to do this effectively. This study compared the impact of multimedia versus audio-based educational interventions on the knowledge and self-reported behavior of general dentists in Tehran regarding nutrition and oral health. METHODS: In this randomized controlled trial, 166 general dentists in Tehran were recruited in 2023 through professional online platforms and randomly allocated to either a multimedia-based or an audio-based educational intervention. Knowledge (11 items) and behavior (9 items) regarding the impact of nutrition on periodontal health, dental caries, oral cancer, and erosion were assessed using a validated questionnaire. The educational intervention was delivered over a one-month period. Within-group changes were assessed using paired t-tests, between-group differences using repeated-measures ANOVA, and the effect of demographic variables on post-intervention scores using ANCOVA, with baseline values as covariates (α = 0.05). RESULTS: Of the participants, 53.6% were women, and 37.9% worked in private practice. Both groups demonstrated significant improvements in knowledge and behavior scores following the intervention (p < 0.001), with greater gains observed in the multimedia group. Analysis of covariance indicated that baseline knowledge and behavior were not significantly associated with age, gender, dental school, years of professional experience, or practice setting. CONCLUSION: Both multimedia- and audio-based educational interventions effectively improved dentists' knowledge and self-reported behaviors related to nutrition and oral health. Therefore, given dentists' busy work schedules, the use of these educational approaches may enhance their capacity to provide evidence-based counseling in the field of nutrition and oral health.

item.dc:creator: Bañeras T, Jiménez-Alvarado D, Toledo-Padilla H, Camps-Lahora L, Castro JJ, Espino-Ruano A, Guerra-Marrero A, Couce-Montero L, Meyers EKM, Bañeras L
item.description:
Authors: Bañeras T, Jiménez-Alvarado D, Toledo-Padilla H, Camps-Lahora L, Castro JJ, Espino-Ruano A, Guerra-Marrero A, Couce-Montero L, Meyers EKM, Bañeras L

Published: 2026-01-01

Abstract:
Shark microbiome studies offer acute insights into host health, immunity, and ecological interactions, yet remain poorly studied compared to other marine vertebrates. Shark-associated microbial communities, despite being species-specific, are influenced by environmental conditions and feeding ecology. In this study, we aimed to characterize shifts in the microbiome of the Critically Endangered angelshark (Squatina squatina) during the early stages of development and to assess how environmental factors contribute to the shaping of a specific microbiota. Samples from thirty-nine juvenile angelsharks were collected from Las Teresitas nursery area in the Canary Islands over one year. Skin, oral and cloacal microbiomes were analysed using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. The sizes of individuals ranged between 24 and 42 cm in length. The shark microbiome was clearly distinct from the surrounding environment, indicating a unique composition from early life stages. Dominant bacteria present in the shark microbiomes included Vibrionaceae (up to 96%), Pseudoalteromonas (up to 63%), Rhodobacteraceae (up to 57%) and Alteromonadaceae (up to 20%). Seawater had a greater influence than sediment on the external skin microbiome, especially in younger individuals. This was not expected due to the burial behaviour of the species. Notably, the abundance of Pseudoalteromonadaceae (assessed by qPCR) was positively correlated with shark growth but was independent of the skin mucus. This suggests a protective role of this phylotype in younger individuals and may help in the adaptation to habitat conditions. This is the first comprehensive microbiome study in angelsharks, highlighting the importance of environmental preservation for microbial integrity and juvenile fitness.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer has been the leading cause of death in Taiwan since 1982, but long-term survival trends remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated 25-year cancer survival trends, including stage-specific outcomes. METHODS: We analyzed Taiwan Cancer Registry data for patients aged 15-99 years diagnosed with cancer between 1996 and 2021. We estimated the cancer survival index for all sites combined and age- and sex-adjusted 5-year relative survival ratios for individual cancers. The Ederer II cohort method was used for diagnoses before 2018, and the survivorship-period-cohort model was used to nowcast survival for diagnoses in 2018-2020. TNM stage-specific survival was evaluated for 17 cancers diagnosed during 2010-2017. RESULTS: The 5-year cancer survival index increased from 46.8% in 1996 to a nowcast estimate of 56.2% in 2020. Survival improved most for small intestine, lung, and nasopharyngeal cancers, with lung adenocarcinoma also shifting toward earlier-stage diagnosis. Survival declined for cervical, renal pelvis, bladder, brain and CNS, and gallbladder cancers. CONCLUSIONS: Nationwide cancer survival improved substantially, but persistent cancer-specific gaps highlight priorities for early detection, treatment, and cancer control. IMPACT: These population-based estimates provide timely evidence for monitoring cancer prognosis, evaluating cancer-control progress, and identifying cancers and stages requiring greater clinical and public health attention.

Published: 2026-Oct-28

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether preoperative intravenous iron infusion is associated with reduced postoperative packed red blood cell (PRBC) transfusion risk and transfusion volume among patients undergoing head and neck free flap reconstruction. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study. SETTING: Tertiary head and neck cancer centre. METHODS: Adult patients undergoing free flap reconstruction for head and neck cancer between January 2022 and May 2025 were included. Starting June 2022, patients with baseline hemoglobin <130 g/L underwent routine preoperative transferrin saturation testing. Patients with transferrin saturation <20% who subsequently received preoperative intravenous iron infusion were compared with those who did not. Primary outcome was receipt of postoperative PRBC transfusion. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess predictors of transfusion. Negative binomial regression was used to model transfusion volume among transfused patients. RESULTS: Among 324 patients, 32 (9.9%) received preoperative intravenous iron and 59 (18.2%) required postoperative PRBC transfusion. Preoperative iron infusion was not independently associated with postoperative transfusion risk (aOR 1.26, 95% CI: 0.51-3.08, P = .62) or with number of PRBC units transfused (aIRR 1.00, 95% CI: 0.41-2.38, P = .997). Higher preoperative hemoglobin was associated with reduced transfusion risk (aOR 0.96 per g/L increase, 95% CI: 0.94-0.98, P < .001), while advanced tumor stage was associated with increased transfusion risk (aOR 2.55, 95% CI: 1.13-5.77, P = .024). These findings were unchanged in sensitivity analysis restricted to patients receiving iron ≥7 days preoperatively. CONCLUSION: Short-term iron repletion alone may be insufficient to mitigate transfusion requirements, highlighting the importance of earlier and/or more comprehensive anemia optimization strategies in this high-risk population.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Oropharyngeal tumors with a propensity for submucosal spread can be difficult to detect and delineate during endoscopy. To facilitate their detection, we developed an Artificial Intelligence (AI) algorithm to segment tumors and other anatomically significant structures within the oropharynx. STUDY DESIGN: Model development and validation study. SETTING: Tertiary academic medical center. METHODS: We collected videos from 106 patients undergoing pharyngolaryngoscopy, extracted 942 images, and annotated each pixel as one of 12 classes, such as tumor, uvula, and healthy mucosa. We trained an AI algorithm and evaluated its performance in multiclass and tumor-based segmentation. RESULTS: The AI algorithm achieved a recall statistic of 0.93 and a Dice score of 0.79 for tumor detection. High Dice scores were observed for pharyngeal mucosa (0.90), epiglottis (0.88), and vocal cords (0.82). CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that AI can semantically segment all the structures visualized during endoscopy, paving the way for computer-assisted systems for tumor identification and computer-assisted navigation during endoscopy or intubation.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy of vidian neurectomy (VN) in improving nasal and ocular symptoms in patients with drug-refractory allergic rhinoconjunctivitis (ARC). STUDY DESIGN: A prospective randomized controlled study. SETTING: Yiyang Central Hospital. METHODS: A total of 220 patients with drug-refractory ARC were allocated to the VN (n = 110) and fluticasone propionate (FP) (n = 110) groups. Clinical data, serum, and tear samples were collected at baseline and at 1 week, 2 weeks, 1 month, and 3 months after treatment. Serum immunoglobulin E (IgE), IgG, and IgA levels, tear meniscus height (TMH), tear break-up time (TBUT), tear secretion (via Schirmer's test [SIT]), and eosinophil cationic protein (ECP) and histamine (HA) were assessed. A 1-year follow-up was conducted to evaluate complications and recurrence, and the Kaplan-Meier curves were plotted to show the recurrence rates. RESULTS: Following treatment, patients in the VN group showed reduced serum IgE, IgG, IgA, ECP, and HA levels, and Visual Analog Scale (VAS), Sino-Nasal Outcome Test-20, Total Nasal Symptom Score, corneal fluorescein staining, and Rhinoconjunctivitis Quality of Life Questionnaire scores, and increased TMH, TBUT, and SIT. Although complications were more frequent in the VN group, the 1-year recurrence rate was lower. CONCLUSION: VN significantly improves nasal and ocular symptoms, reduces immunologic and inflammatory markers, and lowers short-term recurrence in drug-refractory ARC, indicating favorable clinical potential.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We performed an outcome-specific network meta-analysis comparing contemporary energy devices in thyroidectomy. METHODS: Randomized controlled trials comparing conventional hemostasis with Harmonic, LigaSure, Thunderbeat, or other advanced energy devices during thyroidectomy were included. Frequentist random-effects network meta-analyses were performed per outcome, with treatments ranked by P-scores and consistency assessed via design-by-treatment interaction and node-splitting analyses. RESULTS: Compared to conventional hemostasis, Harmonic significantly reduced operative time (SMD, -1.88), blood loss (SMD, -2.29), drainage volume (SMD, -1.77), hospital stay (SMD, -0.74), transient hypocalcemia (OR, 0.61), transient recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy (OR, 0.63), and postoperative bleeding (OR, 0.56). CONCLUSIONS: Harmonic showed the most favorable relative effects across the evaluated outcomes. However, these findings do not establish overall device superiority; selection should consider absolute benefits and device-specific characteristics.

item.title: Targeting Engrailed-1 Fibroblasts in Idiopathic Subglottic Stenosis.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Idiopathic subglottic stenosis (iSGS) is characterized by pathologic deposition of extracellular matrix (ECM) secondary to dysregulated fibroblasts. Engrailed-1 expressing fibroblasts have been shown to promote ECM deposition in fibrosis. Verteporfin has been shown to reduce EN1 expression in fibroblasts through YAP/TAZ signaling. However, EN1 expression, YAP/TAZ signaling, and verteporfin treatment have not been investigated in iSGS pathogenesis. METHODS: Biopsies of diseased subglottis and distal healthy trachea of iSGS patients (n = 6) were assessed. qRT-PCR, analysis of iSGS single-cell RNA sequencing data, flow cytometry and immunochemistry were used to compare the expression of EN1. Fibroblasts from diseased iSGS tissue were treated with verteporfin (5 μM) or control and gene and protein expression analysis was performed for EN1, YAP/TAZ pathway and fibrotic genes. RESULTS: The iSGS subglottis demonstrated increased expression of EN1 (fold change = 58.86, SD = 65.12, p: 0.031) compared to controls. Immunohistochemistry analysis of the diseased iSGS subglottis showed that EN1 was densely expressed. Verteporfin treatment of iSGS fibroblasts in vitro led to an 81.75% (SD = 9.28, p: 0.031) reduction in COL1A1 and 22.77% (SD = 17.11, p: 0.031) reduction in COL3A1 gene expression. CONCLUSION: EN1 and the associated YAP/TAZ signaling pathway are increased in iSGS. Verteporfin treatment inhibited YAP/TAZ expression and attenuated EN1 and COL1A1 expression in vitro. Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether preoperative blood inflammatory ratios discriminate malignant from benign parotid tumours. METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study included 204 patients undergoing parotidectomy (45 malignant, 159 benign); inflammatory-index analyses included 45 malignant and 157 benign cases. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratios were the two primary indices. Group differences were tested non-parametrically with multiplicity control, discrimination by receiver operating characteristic analysis and association by multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: Median neutrophil-to-lymphocyte and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratios were higher in malignant tumours (2.00 vs. 1.81 and 0.203 vs. 0.166), but effect sizes were small. CONCLUSIONS: Although the two primary ratios were higher in malignant tumours, their distributions overlapped substantially and discrimination was poor. These findings do not support their use as stand-alone markers for preoperative malignancy risk stratification.

Multi-organ-system insulin resistance is the key pathogenic driver of obesity-related metabolic complications and diseases, such as atherogenic dyslipidemia, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and type 2 diabetes. However, there is considerable heterogeneity in insulin sensitivity among people with obesity. Some are considered to have metabolically healthy obesity, with normal insulin sensitivity in conjunction with normal fasting blood glucose, oral glucose tolerance, plasma lipid profile and intrahepatic triglyceride content. In this Review, we discuss metabolic differences at the cellular, organ-system and systemic levels between people with metabolically healthy and metabolically unhealthy obesity; we also discuss heterogeneity in the therapeutic effects of weight reduction. A better understanding of the differences between metabolically divergent groups and the physiological responses to weight loss can help identify the factors responsible for the link between excess adiposity and metabolic dysfunction and disease.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To establish a murine heterotopic laryngeal transplantation (LT) model with a single HLA-A2 mismatch and to develop a multidimensional framework for dynamic evaluation of immune rejection and graft injury. METHODS: Laryngeal grafts from HLA-A2 transgenic mice were transplanted into C57BL/6 recipients to generate an HLA-mismatched LT model, with syngeneic C57BL/6 → C57BL/6 transplants as controls. RESULTS: Compared with syngeneic transplantation, the HLA-mismatched group showed aggravated immune rejection and graft injury. Progressive graft volume reduction was an early discriminator, detectable at 1 week posttransplantation and correlating with graft surface darkening and ulceration. Immunophenotyping revealed early CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell infiltration beginning at 1 week, whereas regulatory T cells increased at 3 days before markedly declining. Cytokine profiling showed elevations of MIP-1β, G-CSF, and IL-10 from 4 weeks onward, consistent with immune activation and graft injury. CONCLUSION: A murine heterotopic LT model with an HLA-A2 mismatch was established, demonstrating that a single HLA Class I disparity was sufficient to drive progressive immune rejection and graft injury in LT. Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess whether e-cigarette use is associated with subsequent health symptoms over time among young people in the United States. item.title: Pazopanib alternating with bevacizumab in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to treatment: a multicentre, single-arm, phase 1/2 trial.
