Abstract:
BACKGROUND: VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) are considered the backbone for the treatment of metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. We hypothesise that the administration of bevacizumab during scheduled breaks in pazopanib (TKI) treatment can improve tolerability and prolong progression-free survival compared with historical controls. METHODS: In this single-arm, phase 1/2 trial in five US academic cancer centres, patients (aged ≥18 years) with histologically confirmed metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 or less, and adequate organ functions were included. The phase 1 portion included patients with up to one previous therapy with high-dose IL-2 or an anti-PD-1 compound alone or in combination with a CTLA-4 inhibitor. The phase 2 portion enrolled only patients with treatment-naive metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. The primary endpoint of phase 1 was to find the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D). We tested a novel regimen using four dose levels: oral pazopanib (600 or 800 mg daily on days 1-28, followed by a 7 day break) alternating with intravenous bevacizumab (5, 7·5, or 10 mg/kg, one on day 36 and one on day 50) on a 10-week cycle in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to TKI treatment. The primary endpoint of phase 2 was median progression-free survival, assessed by a masked central statistician review. Dose selection (in patients who had completed 15 weeks) and activity (in patients who had completed one full 10-week cycle of the novel regimen) were analysed in the per-protocol population. Safety analyses included all patients who received any treatment. This trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01684397) and is ongoing but closed to new participants. FINDINGS: Between Nov 21, 2012, and June 11, 2018, phase 1 enrolled 25 patients, with 18 patients evaluable for dose-limiting toxicity during the extended 15-week safety assessment period. The RP2D was established as pazopanib 800 mg daily (days 1-28) and bevacizumab 10 mg/kg on days 36 and 50 of a 10-week cycle. Between Jan 23, 2019, and Oct 19, 2023, phase 2 enrolled 53 patients, of whom 51 (including six from phase 1) were evaluable for activity and 59 were evaluable for safety. 36 (71%) patients were male and 15 (29%) were female, and 48 (94%) patients were White. 33 (65%) patients in phase 2 had favourable risk per the International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium categories. After a median follow-up of 63·7 months (IQR 16·2-73·5), median progression-free survival was 24·8 months (95% CI 17·2-34·3). The most common grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events were hypertension (20 [34%] of 59) and elevated aspartate aminotransferase (seven [12%]) and alanine aminotransferase (ten [17%]). Five (8%) patients discontinued the study for drug-related serious adverse events. No treatment-related deaths occurred. INTERPRETATION: The phase 1 portion identified the safe RP2D. The phase 2 portion showed that this novel regimen has promising antitumour activity in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma in the predominantly favourable risk group who are naive to treatment. Phase 3 randomised controlled trial data are needed to confirm these findings. FUNDING: The Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center (RPCCC), US National Cancer Institute (NCI), Novartis.

item.title: Chemoradiotherapy versus radiotherapy as adjuvant treatment for head and neck adenoid cystic carcinoma: a meta-analysis.

item.description:

Published: 2026-Oct-27

Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The benefit of adding chemotherapy to postoperative radiotherapy for head and neck adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) remains uncertain. We compared adjuvant chemoradiotherapy (CRT) with radiotherapy (RT) alone. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception through May 6, 2026, with manual reference-list checking. Comparative studies reporting time-to-event outcomes for CRT versus RT were eligible. Hazard ratios (HRs) were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and the Hartung-Knapp adjustment. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261485857). RESULTS: Eight studies contributed 836 outcome-specific observations. CRT was not associated with improved overall survival (six studies; 648 patients; HR, 0.99; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.70-1.41; I2 = 0%), disease-free/progression-free survival (five studies; 534 patients; HR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.81-1.34; I2 = 0%), or distant metastasis-free survival (six studies; 574 patients; HR, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.55-1.63; I2 = 44.5%). Neither locoregional control (two studies; 354 patients; HR, 0.09; 95% CI, 0.00-59.00) nor locoregional failure-free survival (three studies; 262 patients; HR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.32-2.60) improved significantly; both estimates were imprecise. Results were consistent in adjusted-versus-unadjusted subgroup and leave-one-out analyses. CONCLUSION: Available nonrandomized evidence does not demonstrate that adjuvant CRT improves survival compared with RT alone in head and neck ACC. Evidence for locoregional outcomes remains sparse and imprecise. These findings do not support routine chemotherapy but favor individualized treatment decisions.

item.title: Competence narrowing in AI-assisted oral English instruction: A quasi-experimental study of the spiral synergy framework.
item.dc:creator: Zhang J
item.description:
Authors: Zhang J
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0357515
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42945343



Abstract:
The rapid integration of generative AI tools into spoken English instruction has produced measurable fluency and accuracy gains, but whether these are evenly distributed across the dimensions of communicative competence remains underexplored. This quasi-experimental study compares the Spiral Synergy Framework (SSF), a three-layer pedagogical sequence (AI Consolidation, Bridging Tasks, Interpersonal Activation), against conventional AI-integrated instruction in two intact Business English classes at a Chinese higher vocational college (experimental n = 36, control n = 34), using oral recordings at three time points scored on five competence dimensions, 15 weeks of classroom observation, and an intra-rater reliability check. The two classes differed significantly at baseline on the oral composite score and three of five dimensions (control higher), though not on CET-4 proficiency or questionnaire items. Because treatment is confounded with class membership and both classes received AI-assisted practice, findings are reported as associations rather than demonstrated causal effects. Linear mixed-effects models testing Group × Time interactions across five outcomes (four dimensions and the composite), corrected for multiple comparisons, identified one outcome - real-time responsiveness - on which the classes diverged: the experimental class maintained responsiveness across the semester while the control class declined despite its baseline advantage (Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted p = .029), a result that held under a cluster-robust sensitivity check. No corrected between-group difference was found for improvisation, coherence, naturalness, or the composite score; improvisation declined descriptively in both classes over the semester. Classroom observation data (experimental class only) document a recurring, non-monotonic cycle of AI-dependency reduction and rebound across 15 weeks. Intra-rater test-retest reliability of the oral-competence ratings was moderate to good (ICC = .67-.91), though this reflects a single rater familiar with participants rather than independent inter-rater agreement. Implications for multidimensional assessment, task sequencing, and cautious interpretation of AI-integrated curriculum research are discussed.

item.title: Safety assessment of microbial Polysaccharide Sanxan.
item.dc:creator: Zhang Y, Wu H, Pi J, Quan G, Chuo Q, Li X, Huang H
item.description:
Authors: Zhang Y, Wu H, Pi J, Quan G, Chuo Q, Li X, Huang H
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361184
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42945291



Abstract:
This study evaluated the oral safety of Sanxan to provide a basis for its application in food. The toxicological characteristics of Sanxan were assessed through an acute oral toxicity test, three genetic toxicity tests, a teratogenicity test in pregnant rats, and a 90-day oral toxicity test. The results showed that no obvious toxic symptoms or mortality were observed in the acute toxicity test, and the maximum tolerated dose was greater than 15 g/kg, indicating that Sanxan had no acute oral toxicity in the test animals. The results of three genetic toxicity tests-the Ames test, the micronucleus test, and the sperm abnormality test-were all negative, and the teratogenicity test in pregnant rats showed no maternal toxicity, embryotoxicity, or teratogenicity, indicating that Sanxan had no mutagenic or teratogenic effects under the tested conditions. The 90-day oral toxicity test showed that Sanxan at doses of 1.3, 2.6, and 5.2 g/kg body weight had no obvious adverse effects on body weight gain, total food intake, total food utilization, hematology, serum biochemistry, organ-to-body weight ratios, or pathological examination in the test animals, and the maximum no-observed-adverse-effect level (NOAEL) was 5.2 g/kg body weight. item.title: Airway management and anaesthetic interventions for children with cleft lip and/or palate undergoing general anaesthesia: Protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.

item.description:
Authors: Sumi SA, Arin KM, Shams SM, Rafique T, Orchi K, Chowdhury A, Rahman MM, Haque MA
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361327
Published: 2026-01-01

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children with cleft lip and/or palate may present unique challenges during perioperative airway management because of altered upper-airway and craniofacial anatomy. These children frequently undergo surgical procedures requiring general anaesthesia and airway instrumentation. Several airway-management and anaesthetic techniques have been evaluated to facilitate tracheal intubation and reduce perioperative airway complications, but the comparative evidence from randomised controlled trials has not been systematically evaluated. METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis will include randomised controlled trials involving children < 18 years with cleft lip and/or palate undergoing general anaesthesia. Eligible studies will compare alternative techniques or devices for airway management or other anaesthetic strategies between two groups of cleft lip/palate patients. The primary outcome will be difficulty in tracheal intubation. Where definitions vary substantially, outcomes will be analysed separately or synthesised narratively. Secondary outcomes will include difficult mask ventilation, oxygen desaturation, airway obstruction, difficult laryngoscopy, first-attempt intubation success, number of intubation attempts, time to successful intubation or airway establishment, failed intubation and other perioperative airway or respiratory adverse events. Two reviewers will independently select RCTs, extract data and assess risk of bias. Risk of bias will be evaluated using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Random-effects meta-analysis will be performed where clinically appropriate. Risk ratios will be used for dichotomous outcomes and mean differences or standardized mean differences for continuous outcomes. Certainty of evidence for important outcomes will be assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Photobiomodulation (LLLT) is used for myogenous temporomandibular disorders (TMD), but longer-term comparative evidence versus stabilization splints alongside structured self-management remains limited. METHODS: This partially randomized controlled study enrolled 66 patients with DC/TMD-diagnosed acute masticatory muscle pain. Forty-four participants consenting to intervention were randomized 1:1 to PBM + SM (660-nm diode laser, twice weekly, 10 sessions) or OS + SM (maxillary stabilization splint worn at night, 8 h/day for 2 months). Both intervention groups received the same SM programme (education, habit modification, and jaw exercises for 2 months). A non-randomized convenience group received SM alone (n = 22). item.title: Buccal and sublingual lyophilised naloxone for opioid overdose reversal: A Phase 1 open-label, random-sequence crossover pharmacokinetic study protocol in healthy volunteers (NalBuc).

item.description:
Authors: Gonzalez Utrilla M, Baker A, Chesney E, Lee K, Emsley R, Strang J
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0347370

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Opioid overdose remains a major global public health emergency, with naloxone being an essential response. Benefit from existing naloxone formulations is limited by barriers to acceptability, fixed dosing, and poor real-world carriage. This study describes the protocol for a Phase 1 exploratory investigation of a novel ultra-portable lyophilised naloxone wafer designed to facilitate constant carriage and enable rapid mucosal absorption. Participants will receive five treatments, each separated by ≥36 hours: buccal naloxone wafer 2 mg, buccal wafer 4 mg, sublingual wafer 2 mg, intramuscular naloxone 0.4 mg, and intranasal naloxone 1.8 mg (Nyxoid®). item.title: Joint Effects of ALDH2 rs671 and Pathogenic Germline Variants in DNA Repair Genes on Risk of Aerodigestive and Gastrointestinal Cancers.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (ALDH2) rs671 (G>A) variant, common in East Asians, impairs aldehyde detoxification. item.title: Helicobacter pylori Infection Is Associated With the Occurrence and Progression of Vocal Fold Leukoplakia via NRF2/KEAP1 Pathway Activation.

Abstract:
Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection has been implicated in vocal fold leukoplakia (VFL), a precancerous laryngeal lesion. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the relationship between H. pylori and VFL, focusing on the NRF2/KEAP1 oxidative stress pathway. Clinicopathological analysis was performed on samples from 64 patients with VFL and 30 patients with vocal cord polyps (controls). The results showed a significantly higher prevalence of H. pylori in the VFL group (48.4%) than in the controls (16.7%, p = 0.003). Among H. pylori-positive VFL cases, VacA-positive strains predominated, accounting for 71.0%. item.title: The Evolution and Clinical Utility of Oral Epithelial Dysplasia Grading Systems: A Narrative Review.
item.dc:creator: Ramanathan A, Tilakaratne WM
item.description:
Authors: Ramanathan A, Tilakaratne WM
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70553
Published: 2026-Oct-27
PMID: 42935262



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Histological grading of oral epithelial dysplasia (OED) is the gold standard for predicting malignant transformation in potentially malignant disorders. However, traditional grading systems suffer from subjectivity and poor diagnostic reproducibility, complicating patient management. This narrative review evaluates the clinical utility of current and emerging OED grading systems. METHODS: We reviewed recent literature (2019-2026) comparing the traditional World Health Organization (WHO) classifications against binary grading, histopathological feature-specific models (two-point and six-point systems), diagnostic biomarkers, and clinical risk factors. RESULTS: The WHO system frequently demonstrates poor-to-fair interobserver agreement. Conversely, binary and six-point grading systems provide superior reproducibility. While these models effectively stratify malignant transformation risk, their clinical utility is limited by tissue sampling errors, such as "skip areas." Furthermore, immunohistochemical biomarkers (Keratin 13 and 17) show promise as diagnostic adjuncts to assist in identifying high-risk variants like differentiated dysplasia. CONCLUSION: While the WHO system remains the gold standard, its subjectivity complicates clinical decisions. Adopting objective binary and feature-specific models offers superior clinical utility for risk stratification. Clear numerical cutoffs alongside expanded morphological features and biomarkers may influence the accuracy of predicting malignant transformation, inform clinical decision-making regarding surgical versus conservative surveillance, and optimize patient management when integrated with clinicopathological findings.

item.title: Recurrence Risk in Lateralized Floor of Mouth Carcinoma: Depth of Invasion Versus Midline Distance.
item.dc:creator: Ketschau J, Grabenhorst A, Singer H, Kram H, Krautkremer N, Leopold C, Mohr J, Pippich K, Wolff KD, Ohayon C, et al.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contralateral nodal recurrence in lateralized floor-of-mouth squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remains difficult to predict, and objective preoperative parameters to guide contralateral neck management in tumors without midline crossing are lacking. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 97 patients with lateral floor-of-mouth OSCC treated by surgical resection and neck dissection. Depth of invasion (DOI) was evaluated using endpoint-specific univariable Cox regression. Contralateral nodal disease was analyzed in patients without midline crossing (n = 68) using a composite endpoint of occult contralateral nodal metastasis and/or subsequent contralateral nodal recurrence. Tumor-to-midline distance was assessed on standardized multiplanar preoperative CT or MRI. RESULTS: DOI was associated with local recurrence (HR 1.322 per mm, 95% CI 1.131-1.545, p < 0.001) and ipsilateral regional recurrence (HR 1.199, 95% CI 1.052-1.367, p = 0.007), but not with contralateral recurrence (HR 1.030, 95% CI 0.834-1.272, p = 0.782). Four patients (5.9%) developed subsequent contralateral nodal recurrence. Midline distance was smaller in patients with an event (median 3.15 vs. 6.40 mm; p = 0.022; AUC 0.845). CONCLUSION: DOI showed an outcome-specific association with local and ipsilateral, but not contralateral, recurrence. In tumors without midline crossing, quantitative proximity to the midline was associated with subsequent contralateral nodal failure. OBJECTIVES: Cancer cells reprogram glucose metabolism toward aerobic glycolysis, a phenomenon known as the Warburg effect. This metabolic shift results in substantial lactate accumulation within the tumor microenvironment. Although lactate has been implicated in tumor aggressiveness, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. In vitro functional assays and xenograft studies were performed using GPR81-knockdown HSC-3 and SAS cell lines. item.title: Epidemiological characterization of avian influenza virus circulation in pigeons and quail across different production systems in Chattogram, Bangladesh.

Abstract:
Pigeons and quail contribute to poultry production, nutrition, and livelihoods in Bangladesh; however, their role in avian influenza virus (AIV) circulation remains poorly understood. These poultry species are widely reared and traded alongside chickens and ducks in household farms, commercial systems, and live bird markets, where inadequate biosecurity may create an overlooked ecological niche for AIV circulation, reassortment, and potential zoonotic spillover. A total of 300 birds (108 pigeons and 192 quail) were sampled from households, commercial farms, and live bird markets. Oropharyngeal and cloacal swabs were collected from each bird and tested for the AIV matrix gene using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction, followed by subtype-specific detection of H5, H7, and H9. Data collected from bird owners and traders included bird demographic characteristics, bird source, and health status using a structured questionnaire. The overall prevalence of AIV was 14.3% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 10.6-18.8). Quail had a higher prevalence (18.2%, 95% CI: 13.0-24.4) than pigeons (7.4%, 95% CI: 3.3-14.1). item.title: Oral versus vaginal Lactobacillus supplementation for endometrial dysbiosis: A paired pre and post-endometrial microbiome study.

Abstract:
Infertility is a global health challenge, and impaired endometrial receptivity remains an important contributor to treatment failure. Endometrial dysbiosis, characterized by a low proportion of Lactobacillus in the endometrial microbiota, has been proposed as a potentially modifiable factor that may affect endometrial receptivity and fertility, and treatment with Lactobacillus-containing probiotics is emerging as a promising therapeutic approach. item.title: The combination of simethicone and N-acetylcysteine in lidocaine ice popsicle compared with lidocaine ice popsicle alone in patients undergoing unsedated esophagogastroduodenoscopy: A prospective double-blind randomized controlled trial.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal mucosal visualization is essential for high-quality esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD), particularly for the detection of subtle upper gastrointestinal lesions. Oral simethicone and N-acetylcysteine (NAC) are commonly used to improve mucosal cleanliness, whereas lidocaine ice popsicles provide effective topical pharyngeal anesthesia for unsedated EGD. We evaluated whether incorporating simethicone and NAC into a lidocaine ice popsicle could improve mucosal visibility while maintaining patient comfort. METHODS: This single-center, prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled trial enrolled 374 adults undergoing unsedated diagnostic EGD between December 2024 and June 2025. Participants were randomized (1:1) to receive either a lidocaine ice popsicle containing simethicone (100 mg) and NAC (600 mg) or a conventional lidocaine ice popsicle. Secondary outcomes included procedure time, water volume required for mucosal cleansing, additional simethicone use, endoscopist satisfaction, ease of esophageal instrumentation, gag reflex, patient satisfaction, discomfort, pain, and adverse events. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 25.0 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA). RESULTS: All 374 randomized participants (187 per group) completed the study and were analyzed according to their assigned groups. Baseline characteristics were descriptively similar between groups. The intervention group had a significantly lower TVS than the control group (6.19 ± 0.51 vs. 10.39 ± 2.22; mean difference, -4.20; 95% CI, -4.53 to -3.88; P < 0.001), indicating better mucosal visibility. Exploratory segment-specific analyses showed lower visibility scores in all six gastrointestinal segments. The intervention group also had higher endoscopist satisfaction, shorter procedure time (10.87 ± 1.44 vs. 12.75 ± 0.96 min; P < 0.001), lower water requirements for mucosal cleansing, and less frequent use of additional diluted simethicone during EGD (12.8% vs. 96.8%; P < 0.001). Exploratory analyses showed statistically significant differences in gag reflex and pain scores, although the absolute differences were small. Patient satisfaction, discomfort, and ease of esophageal instrumentation did not differ significantly between groups. No adverse events were observed during the defined observation period. CONCLUSIONS: The combined formulation of simethicone and N-acetylcysteine incorporated into a lidocaine ice popsicle improved mucosal visibility compared with a lidocaine ice popsicle alone during unsedated EGD and was associated with improved procedural efficiency. Further multicenter studies are warranted to confirm its effectiveness, generalizability, and safety with longer follow-up. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Thai Clinical Trials Registry TCTR20240606004.

item.title: Low- and intermediate-grade, low-stage primary parotid cancer: does a "partial" surgery impair disease control? a multicenter retrospective study.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Primary parotid malignancies are rare and heterogeneous. While comprehensive surgery with postoperative radiotherapy (PORT) is well established for high-grade and/or advanced-stage disease, the optimal management of lower grade, early-stage parotid carcinomas remains debatable due to their indolent behavior and low risk of nodal spread. METHODS: A multicenter retrospective analysis was conducted across ten tertiary referral centers. Patients with primary parotid carcinomas staged as pT1-T2 cN0/pNx and classified as low/intermediate-grade were included (2000-2020). Surgical procedures were categorized as partial (extracapsular dissection, partial superficial, superficial, selective deep lobe parotidectomy) or comprehensive. Time to recurrence (TTR), recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) were analyzed. RESULTS: A total of 129 patients met the inclusion criteria. Partial surgery was performed in 75.4% of cases, and PORT was administered in 37.8%. The 5-year TTR, RFS and OS was 96.6%, 91.7%, and 94.9%, respectively. Recurrence occurred in 3.9% of patients, with no regional failures and no disease-related deaths. PNI was linked to shorter TTR (HR 17.3, p = 0.002), whereas intermediate grade (HR 3.17, p = 0.035), older age (HR 1.03, p = 0.050), pT2 (HR 2.96, p = 0.045) and PNI (HR 4.68, p = 0.009) were associated with lower RFS. item.description:

Published: 2026-Oct-26
PMID: 42931838



Abstract:
PURPOSE: This systematic review evaluates the relative safety and side-effect profiles of endotracheal tubes (ETs) and supraglottic airway devices (SGAs) for airway management in endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS). METHODS: A search of MEDLINE, Embase and the Cochrane Library was conducted in April 2025. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed for outcomes reported by three or more studies with comparable methodology; remaining outcomes were synthesised narratively. Primary outcomes were aspiration events, airway contamination and adverse post-operative symptoms (cough, sore throat, hoarseness, nausea and vomiting); secondary outcomes were operative time and estimated blood loss. Nine studies (714 patients, 1995-2024) were eligible. RESULTS: Aspiration was rare (one asymptomatic ET case). Pooled analysis demonstrated a significant reduction in airway contamination with SGA use (RR 0.27, 95% CI 0.15-0.47, I²=0%). Device contamination was common in both (SGAs 0-86%, ETs 53-77%) but of limited clinical consequence. Pooled analysis also demonstrated a significant reduction in post-operative day 0 cough with SGA use (RR 0.39, 95% CI 0.23-0.68, I²=0%), whereas day 0 sore throat showed no significant difference (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.24-1.74, I²=68.7%). Trends toward reduced hoarse voice, blood loss and operative time favoured SGAs but were not significant. CONCLUSION: The historical concern that SGAs offer inferior airway protection during ESS is not supported by current comparative evidence. In appropriately selected, low-aspiration-risk patients, SGAs represent a safe alternative to ETs. Given the heterogeneous evidence base, findings should assist rather than replace clinical judgment, with device selection guided by individual patient and procedural factors.

item.title: Effects of aging and bolus characteristics on laryngeal movement during oropharyngeal swallowing.
item.dc:creator: Lee SH, Hsieh LC, Yan JY, Lee GS
item.description:
Authors: Lee SH, Hsieh LC, Yan JY, Lee GS
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10686-y
Published: 2026-Oct-26
PMID: 42931835



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Swallowing is a complex sensorimotor process that dynamically adapts to bolus characteristics and physiological variations. Age-related neuromuscular changes in older adults can alter swallowing function, potentially compromising swallowing safety and efficiency. This study investigated age-related differences in oropharyngeal swallowing by analyzing laryngeal displacement and swallowing sounds using a force-sensitive resistor (FSR) sensor and cervical auscultation. METHODS: Six swallowing tasks with varying bolus volumes and viscosities were assessed across 16 healthy young adults and 12 healthy older adults. A two-way mixed-model repeated-measures analysis of variance was conducted to examine differences in temporal and amplitude parameters of the acoustic and FSR signals. RESULTS: FSR signals analysis revealed that increasing bolus volumes shorten the duration of laryngeal activation in young adults, whereas it produced significantly prolonged laryngeal activation in older adults. Additionally, aging significantly increased the overall duration of laryngeal movement during swallowing, particularly during the relaxation phase. No significant gender effects were observed in any of the analyses. CONCLUSIONS: In older adults, slower laryngeal movement during the oropharyngeal phase of swallowing indicates reduced muscular capacity and diminished coordination between bolus transit and laryngeal kinematics. These age-related neuromuscular changes may compromise swallowing efficiency and airway protection, thereby increasing susceptibility to dysphagia-related complications. Future research should focus on developing automated detection algorithms and multimodal datasets that combine physiological measurements and swallowing imaging to objectively link sensor-derived features to physiological swallowing events.

item.title: Fat graft-reinforced repair of refractory cervical chyle leak after neck dissection.
item.dc:creator: Roh JL
item.description:
Authors: Roh JL

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Chyle leak is an uncommon but clinically significant complication after neck dissection, particularly in the left lower neck, where the thoracic duct is most vulnerable. High-output or persistent leakage may result in metabolic derangement, wound complications, and delayed recovery. Surgical intervention becomes necessary when conservative management is unsuccessful. This study describes a standardized surgical technique combining targeted lymphatic ligation with autologous abdominal fat graft reinforcement and reports its clinical outcomes. METHODS: Five patients who developed refractory or high-output chyle leak after neck dissection at a university hospital cancer center underwent surgical repair. Conservative measures, including dietary fat restriction, pressure dressing, closed suction drainage, and octreotide, were employed before surgery. Operative management consisted of precisely identifying the leaking lymphatic channel, ligation with 4 - 0 polypropylene sutures, and placement of a peri-umbilical fat graft to reinforce the repair. RESULTS: All patients showed immediate cessation of chyle leakage following surgery. None required reoperation, thoracic duct embolization, or thoracoscopic intervention. A regular oral diet was resumed within 3-5 days, and all patients were discharged without complications. Follow-up assessments confirmed durable resolution without recurrence or donor-site morbidity. CONCLUSION: Targeted lymphatic ligation combined with autologous fat grafting reinforcement was technically feasible and was associated with successful leak control in this small descriptive case series. item.title: Head and neck cancer in older adults: biological aging, treatment tolerance, and survivorship.
item.dc:creator: Bou Zerdan M, Assi J, Bouferraa Y, Abu Faraj J, Bilani N, Brammer B, Castro EA, Abi Zeid Daou C, Stokes WA, Rudra S, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Bou Zerdan M, Assi J, Bouferraa Y, Abu Faraj J, Bilani N, Brammer B, Castro EA, Abi Zeid Daou C, Stokes WA, Rudra S, et al.
Journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute | DOI: 10.1093/jnci/djag332
Published: 2026-Oct-26

Abstract:
Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNC) is increasingly diagnosed in older adults, a population characterized by substantial heterogeneity in physiologic reserve, comorbidity burden, functional status, and social support. Chronological age alone is an inadequate predictor of treatment tolerance and outcomes, yet it continues to influence therapeutic decision-making despite growing evidence supporting individualized assessment. This review summarizes the current evidence on aging and HNC, emphasizing the impact of comorbidities, frailty, comprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA), and biological aging on treatment selection, toxicity, and survival. We review validated geriatric assessment tools, including frailty measures and evaluation of cognitive, nutritional, and social domains, which consistently provide prognostic information beyond age and conventional performance status. Emerging data on immunologic aging and other biomarkers of biological aging suggest promising avenues for improving risk stratification, although these approaches remain investigational. We also discuss evidence from contemporary clinical trials, treatment adaptation and de-escalation strategies, implementation science, and the persistent underrepresentation of older adults in oncology research. Survivorship challenges, including late toxicities, functional decline, rehabilitation, and multidisciplinary long-term care, are reviewed alongside disparities in access to care that disproportionately affect older patients. Collectively, the available evidence supports a shift from age-based treatment decisions toward individualized care guided by physiologic reserve, geriatric assessment, and patient-centered goals. Future progress will depend on integrating geroscience, validated biomarkers of biological aging, geriatric-informed clinical trial design, and implementation strategies that improve equitable access to evidence-based care for the growing population of older adults with HNC.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Temporalis muscle flap (TMF) reconstruction is common for postradiation skull base osteoradionecrosis (ORN). Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To critically synthesize and integrate intraoperative technical strategies designed to optimize visualization, surgical exposure, tissue protection, and/or hemostatic control during adenotonsillar surgery. METHODS: A structured narrative review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and the Cochrane Library to identify studies published between January 1996 and May 2026. The search strategy combined MeSH terms and free-text keywords related to adenotonsillectomy, operative visualization, surgical exposure, hemostasis, tissue protection, microscopy, endoscopy, and suction-assisted techniques. Following title and abstract screening and full-text assessment, 38 studies were included in the final qualitative synthesis. RESULTS: The available evidence indicates that multiple complementary intraoperative strategies can improve operative precision and surgical safety during adenotonsillar surgery. Microscope- and endoscope-assisted techniques enhance anatomical visualization, facilitate targeted hemostasis, and improve the identification of residual lymphoid tissue and occult bleeding sites. Cheek expanders and modified retraction systems increase transverse surgical exposure and improve instrument maneuverability. Protective measures, including salivary cotton rolls and moist gauze, may reduce pressure- and thermal-related mucosal injury involving the oral commissures, uvula, and posterior pharyngeal wall. Mirror-assisted visualization and soft palate retraction using a Nelaton catheter optimize nasopharyngeal inspection during adenoidectomy. Additional hemostatic measures, including topical vasoconstrictors, gauze packing, warm saline irrigation, continuous suction, and suction coagulation, may reduce intraoperative bleeding while minimizing unnecessary thermal injury. CONCLUSIONS: Optimizing adenotonsillar surgery extends beyond the choice of surgical device. Simple, inexpensive, and reproducible technical modifications can substantially improve visualization, surgical exposure, hemostatic control, tissue preservation, and operative ergonomics, thereby contributing to safer, more standardized, and potentially more effective surgical procedures.

item.title: A senescence-driven fibroblast-macrophage feed-forward circuit promotes radiation induced cutaneous fibrosis.
item.dc:creator: Chung EJ, Kc S, Kwon S, White A, Chung JY, Jung Y, Ahn H, Zhang H, Cauley E, Citrin DE

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Therapeutic radiation for superficial tumors may cause cutaneous fibrosis, a late side effect with limited treatment options. Here, we investigated the underlying mechanisms driving radiation-induced cutaneous fibrosis. METHODS AND MATERIALS: C3H/HeN mice received 35 Gy unilateral hind limb irradiation. Cutaneous tissues from irradiated and contralateral unirradiated legs were analyzed by spatial whole transcriptome profiling using the GeoMx Digital Spatial Profiler platform. Beginning at 5 weeks after irradiation, mice received the senolytic agent ABT-263 (50 mg/kg/day) or vehicle (n ≥ 10/group) by oral gavage (5 consecutive days followed by 2-week rest for 3 cycles). Hind limb contracture was assessed at 150 days after irradiation. Senescence and macrophage markers were evaluated by immunohistochemistry and quantitative PCR. Cellular senescence and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) factors were evaluated in irradiated fibroblasts and their culture media using senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity assays and multiplex immunoassays. The senolytic activity of ABT-263 in irradiated primary fibroblasts and effects of ABT-263 on primary macrophage cultures were evaluated in vitro. RESULTS: Spatial whole-transcriptomic analysis of irradiated murine dermis identified expression patterns consistent with macrophage activation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)-rich environment. In vitro studies identified that the irradiated fibroblast-derived SASP induced a senescent phenotype in unirradiated fibroblasts and macrophages. SASP-induced senescent-like macrophages acquired a CD206+ profibrotic phenotype and in concert with activated fibroblasts, initiated a feed-forward loop amplifying IL-6 and collagen production. SASP exposure increased expression of Bcl-2 family proteins in macrophages and fibroblasts, rendering both populations susceptible to clearance by the senolytic agent ABT-263. item.title: Phase II Study of Neoadjuvant Cemiplimab for Stage II to IV Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Final Analysis.

item.description:
Authors: Gross ND, Miller DM, Khushalani NI, Divi V, Ruiz ES, Lipson EJ, Meier F, Su YB, Swiecicki PL, Atlas J, et al.

Abstract:
We previously reported the results of a multicenter phase II trial (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04154943) of neoadjuvant cemiplimab in resectable stage II to IV cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC), in which the pathologic complete response (pCR) rate was 51%. At the 19-month follow-up, estimated 12-month event-free survival (EFS) was 89%, with 11 EFS events. In this study, we report final EFS and overall survival (OS) at a median follow-up of 54 months. Overall, 16 EFS events occurred at final analysis. There were no new disease recurrence events. The five new EFS events were all comorbidity-related deaths without CSCC recurrence. item.title: Modeling the survival impact of the Inflation Reduction Act out-of-pocket cap in multiple myeloma.
item.dc:creator: Zhao H, Teng S, Dong C, Meng Z, Tan Q, Wang R, Ji M, Schoen MW, Sanfilippo KM, Fiala MA, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Zhao H, Teng S, Dong C, Meng Z, Tan Q, Wang R, Ji M, Schoen MW, Sanfilippo KM, Fiala MA, et al.
Journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute | DOI: 10.1093/jnci/djag396
Published: 2026-Oct-23
PMID: 42924351



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral immunomodulatory imide drugs (IMiDs) have become standard of care for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (NDMM), but high out-of-pocket (OOP) costs may hinder treatment adherence. In 2025, the Inflation Reduction Act introduced a $2,000 annual OOP cost cap (IRAOOPcap) for Medicare Part D beneficiaries. In the absence of post-implementation data, we used comparative modeling to predict its survival impact. METHODS: The survival submodels of two independent Cancer Intervention and Surveillance Modeling Network (CISNET) natural history of multiple myeloma models were used. The models were parameterized using data from Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER)-Medicare, 2012-2021. We simulated survival among Medicare Part D beneficiaries with NDMM aged 66-75 and ≥76 years, under hypothetical scenarios shifting 0% (pre-IRAOOPcap) to 100% (best-case) of patients to IMiD use with high adherence and a realistic scenario using published data. We computed life-years gained (LYG) by comparing life expectancy (LE) under each scenario with that of the pre-IRAOOPcap scenario. RESULTS: Across models, the realistic/best-case scenario yielded LYG of 0.17-0.18/1.10-1.35 among patients aged 66-75 years, and 0.20-0.26/1.29-1.53 for those aged ≥76 years. These translated into 4,164-5,005/26,893-32,347 LYG at the population level for beneficiaries with NDMM in 2025. CONCLUSION: The IRAOOPcap may improve survival through increasing IMiD utilization and adherence among Medicare Part D beneficiaries with NDMM. The projected gains represent a meaningful proportion of contemporary survival for patients. Future research should validate these gains when real-world data are available and inform future policy adaptation and extension.

item.title: The Use of Combination Palliative Radiotherapy and Single-Agent Immunotherapy for the Management of Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (HNSCC) in the United Kingdom (UK).
item.dc:creator: Hurt C, Park S, Chambers J, Brammer C, Griffin M, Harilal V, Stone R, Haris PA, Shakir R, Karsera L, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Hurt C, Park S, Chambers J, Brammer C, Griffin M, Harilal V, Stone R, Haris PA, Shakir R, Karsera L, et al.
Journal: International journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1002/ijc.70802
Published: 2026-Oct-23
PMID: 42922198



Abstract:
Clinical data on combined Immunotherapy (IO) and palliative radiotherapy (RT) in HNSCC is scarce. HNSCC Palliative RT differs from curative intent RT as it does not involve elective nodal irradiation; therefore, an immune response may be more likely. We conducted a UK retrospective survey of patients starting palliative RT and IO monotherapy within 3 months of each other. About 75 patients were treated at 16 centres from January 2022 to December 31, 2023. About 89.3% received first-line Pembrolizumab and 10.7% second-line Nivolumab. 13.3% reported ≥ Grade 3 immune-related adverse events and 6.7% ≥ Grade 3 RTOG side effects; overall response rate (ORR) was 41.3%. Median overall survival (OS) was 10.2 months (95% CI: 6.5-16.2) and median progression-free survival (PFS) was 5.6 months (95% CI: 4.8-8.3). OS was significantly better in locally advanced disease non-amenable to radical treatment (OS HR = 0.42 (95% CI: 0.18-0.97), p = 0.043) and de-novo metastatic disease (OS HR = 0.35 (95% CI: 0.16-0.76), p = 0.008) compared to recurrent disease. Compared to starting IO > 6 weeks after radiotherapy initiation, OS was significantly better in those starting IO 0-6 weeks after radiotherapy initiation (OS HR = 0.40 (95% CI: 0.17-0.95), p = 0.037). The ORR in this cohort is higher than published data of single agent IO alone. Improved survival outcomes in patients receiving IO closer to RT with BED > 70 and alternative fractionation may reflect favourable patient selection but could be influenced by synergy between IO and RT. These findings are from non-randomised cohort data and should be seen as exploratory and hypothesis generating.

item.title: Transcriptomic Convergence Reveals Tumour-Specific Stromal Remodelling in Immune-Enriched Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Petkova V, Dodova R, Vidinov K, Kaneva R
item.description:
Authors: Petkova V, Dodova R, Vidinov K, Kaneva R
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18203406
Published: 2026-Oct-21
PMID: 42938938



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although immune activation can occur in both papillary thyroid carcinoma (TC) and nodular goitre (NG), the transcriptional programmes distinguishing malignant from non-malignant immune-rich thyroid tissue remain poorly understood. METHODS: In this pilot study, bulk RNA sequencing of 19 specimens (10 TC, 9 NG) allowed classification into four tumour microenvironment (TME) subgroups. RESULTS: Immune deconvolution showed that TC Immune-Enriched tumours were characterised by cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) enrichment rather than predominant lymphocytic infiltration. Differential expression analysis identified only nine genes distinguishing TC Immune-Enriched from NG Immune-High tissue, suggesting transcriptomic similarity between malignant and benign immune-activated states in this small cohort. To identify tumour-associated stromal programmes, we identified genes shared between immune-enriched versus immune-depleted comparisons in papillary TC and nodular goitre. This yielded a 441-gene candidate tumour-associated stromal programme enriched for collagen-containing extracellular matrix organisation and TGFβ-associated ECM-remodelling pathways, supported by WGCNA and protein-protein interaction analyses. In 456 TCGA-THCA carcinomas, stromal enrichment correlated inversely with thyroid differentiation and was highest in BRAF-like tumours and the tall-cell histological variant. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that transcriptomic convergence largely reflects shared inflammatory programmes, whereas stromal remodelling identifies a candidate tumour-associated stromal programme.

item.title: Immune Cell Engagers and "Masking Immunotherapy" for Solid Tumors: Focus on Head and Neck Cancers.
item.dc:creator: Nardo G, Lenoci D, Lucchetta M, Licitra L, De Cecco L, Cavalieri S
item.description:
Authors: Nardo G, Lenoci D, Lucchetta M, Licitra L, De Cecco L, Cavalieri S
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18203401
Published: 2026-Oct-21
PMID: 42938933



Abstract:
Head and neck squamous cell carcinomas (HNSCCs) are challenging pathologies to treat with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), as only a minority of patients achieve durable clinical benefit. The highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), the frequent loss of antigen presentation, the marked spatial heterogeneity, and the anatomical proximity of tumors to critical structures limit the efficacy and safety of current immunotherapeutic approaches. Immune cell engagers (ICEs) have emerged as promising strategies to redirect endogenous immune cells toward tumor targets. While conventional surface-antigen-directed engagers can bypass major histocompatibility complex (MHC)-restricted antigen presentation, peptide-HLA-directed constructs remain dependent on antigen processing, peptide presentation, and the appropriate HLA allele. More recently, tumor-restricted activation technologies, collectively referred to as "masking immunotherapy", have been developed to preferentially restore target and/or immune-cell engagement under TME-associated conditions, such as increased protease activity. These approaches have demonstrated enhanced tumor-preferential activity and/or improved tolerability in preclinical models; however, the extent to which these properties translate into clinically meaningful tumor selectivity and an improved therapeutic index remains under investigation. In this review, based on the authors' comprehensive literature knowledge and targeted searches, we critically examine the biological rationale, the engineering principles, the current preclinical evidence, and the early clinical development of ICEs with particular emphasis on their potential application in HNSCC. While early clinical studies have demonstrated acceptable safety profiles, clinical activity has generally been poor. We discuss the major barriers that limit clinical translation and we highlight emerging strategies aimed at overcoming these limitations. We believe that successful clinical development of ICEs in HNSCC will likely depend not only on the identification of optimal target antigens, but also on spatially controlled immune activation, integration with TME-modulating approaches, and incorporation of dynamic biomarkers into future clinical trial design.

item.title: Salvage Surgery with Intraoperative Electron Radiation Therapy for Recurrent or Persistent Head and Neck Cancer After Prior Radiotherapy.
item.dc:creator: Elguindy AN, Baliga S, Klamer BG, Palmiero A, Dibs KN, Koempel A, Gogineni E, Konieczkowski D, Mitchell DL, Seim N, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Elguindy AN, Baliga S, Klamer BG, Palmiero A, Dibs KN, Koempel A, Gogineni E, Konieczkowski D, Mitchell DL, Seim N, et al.
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18203399
Published: 2026-Oct-21
PMID: 42938931



Abstract:
Background/Objectives: Locoregionally recurrent or persistent head and neck cancer (rpHNC) after prior radiotherapy carries a poor prognosis, and optimal salvage strategies remain uncertain. We evaluated survival, patterns of failure, and 90-day postoperative complications after salvage surgery combined with intraoperative electron radiation therapy (IOERT). Methods: We retrospectively identified 127 previously irradiated patients treated with salvage surgery and IOERT between 1999 and 2023. Overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and locoregional failure (LRF) and distant failure were estimated using Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence with death as a competing event. Associations were evaluated one predictor at a time in age- and sex-adjusted Cox (OS, DFS) and Fine-Gray (LRF) models without multiplicity adjustment, and they are exploratory. Results: With a median follow-up of 70 months, median overall survival (OS) was 20.5 months (95% CI, 14.6-40.2), with 1-, 2-, and 3-year OS rates of 63%, 48%, and 43%, respectively. Median disease-free survival (DFS) was 8.8 months. Positive surgical margins and extranodal extension (ENE) were associated with worse OS in separate age- and sex-adjusted models. The 1-, 2-, and 3-year cumulative incidences of LRF were 34.3%, 44.7%, and 49.8%, respectively. The corresponding cumulative incidences of distant failure were 21.6%, 24.0%, and 26.7%, respectively. Thirty-seven patients had a documented distant failure, of whom 27 (73%) experienced distant failure within one year. Available records documented three deaths within 90 days (3/127, 2.4%). Conclusions: Among rpHNC patients treated with this IOERT-containing multimodality salvage strategy, median OS was 20.5 months. Because the study lacked a salvage-surgery-only comparator, postoperative treatments were selectively administered, and complication reporting was incomplete, neither the efficacy nor the comparative safety of IOERT can be determined from these data.

item.title: Anatomical Extent, Presentation, and Outcomes of Distant Metastases to the Infratemporal Fossa: A Systematic Review.
item.dc:creator: Bayramoglu AR, Erginoglu U, Sulaimanov U, Sanlier N, Uslu I, Hamzaoglu C, Kamar Z, Serikkanov Y, Mamadaliev DM, Jalolova M, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Bayramoglu AR, Erginoglu U, Sulaimanov U, Sanlier N, Uslu I, Hamzaoglu C, Kamar Z, Serikkanov Y, Mamadaliev DM, Jalolova M, et al.
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18203392
Published: 2026-Oct-20
PMID: 42938924



Abstract:
Background/Objectives: Distant metastasis to the infratemporal fossa (ITF) is rare and can mimic primary skull-base tumors. We systematically reviewed reported distant ITF metastases. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020 (PROSPERO CRD420261422546), PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched through 12 June 2026, for reports of ITF metastasis from a distant primary tumor; direct extension from adjacent tumors was excluded. Data were summarized descriptively, and reports were appraised with the JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Case Reports. Results: Seventeen reports (17 patients) were included (median age 59 years). The lung was the most frequent primary site (n = 4), followed by the kidney, colorectum, and thyroid (n = 3 each); adenocarcinoma was the most common histology (n = 7). Facial pain (n = 9) and numbness (n = 6) predominated. Bone destruction was reported in 12 patients, and the maxillary sinus (n = 7), orbit (n = 6), pterygopalatine fossa (n = 5), middle cranial fossa (n = 5), and cavernous sinus (n = 4) were involved. The median reported interval to ITF metastasis was 36 months; 11 metastases were metachronous, and 11 patients had other metastatic disease during the reported course. Five patients underwent regional resection or debulking; radiotherapy was reported in eight, radioiodine in three, and systemic drug treatment in nine. At last follow-up, 11 patients were alive, four had died, and status was unknown in two. Conclusions: Distant ITF metastases may present with facial pain and cranial neuropathies. Prognosis is insufficiently characterized, and management should be individualized within a multidisciplinary team. The evidence is limited to case reports with incomplete reporting. No external funding was received.

item.title: A Water-Soluble Pro-Drug of Acetaminophen Has Increased Intracellular Delivery of Active Drug and Anti-Cancer Activity in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer and Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Bryan A, Pangeni R, Akakpo JY, Wendling A, Isbell M, Martin RK, Weistroffer G, Jaeschke H, Ingabire D, Lee WS, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Bryan A, Pangeni R, Akakpo JY, Wendling A, Isbell M, Martin RK, Weistroffer G, Jaeschke H, Ingabire D, Lee WS, et al.
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18203390
Published: 2026-Oct-20
PMID: 42938922



Abstract:
Background/Objectives. Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) are two of the deadliest adult cancers. High-dose acetaminophen (AAP) has anti-cancer activity when given in conjunction with CYP2E1 inhibitors to block liver toxicity. However, the administration of high doses of AAP presents practical challenges stemming from limited water solubility, making it difficult to create a concentrated treatment solution in limited volume. Propacetamol (PROP) is a water-soluble AAP pro-drug that has been used clinically as an IV AAP formulation for analgesia. Methods. We sought to investigate the pharmacokinetics, safety and anti-cancer activity of PROP in comparison to AAP using transplantable syngeneic models of TNBC and PDAC. Results. In vivo, PROP was rapidly converted to AAP within minutes of administration. PROP demonstrated enhanced effectiveness in suppressing tumor growth in the TNBC and PDAC syngeneic murine tumor models compared to AAP. The enhanced efficacy of PROP appears to stem from increased cellular uptake, leading to intracellular AAP concentrations that are 2.7-fold higher within 5 min compared to cells treated with unmodified AAP. PROP demonstrated enhanced modulation of intracellular JAK/STAT signaling, a key mediator of AAP anti-cancer activity, using both murine and humanized models. STAT3 and STAT6 inhibition by PROP led to modulation of macrophage polarization, likely contributing to its anti-TNBC and anti-PDAC activity. While parenteral administration is the preferred route of administration for PROP in anti-cancer indications, we also evaluated the safety and efficacy of oral PROP in comparison to AAP. High-dose PROP demonstrated improved safety following oral administration compared to AAP in the BALB/c murine model while maintaining anti-cancer activity in vivo. Conclusions. PROP, an AAP pro-drug, demonstrates enhanced intracellular delivery of AAP and in vivo anti-cancer activity compared to unmodified AAP, setting the stage for investigation as an anti-cancer drug across different indications.

item.title: Impact of lymph node yield in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck.
item.dc:creator: Fassler CA, Meci A, Patel S, Arnaud EH, Sanchez LJ, Sinard RJ, King TS, Goyal N, Topf MC

Authors: Fassler CA, Meci A, Patel S, Arnaud EH, Sanchez LJ, Sinard RJ, King TS, Goyal N, Topf MC

Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the impact of lymph node yield (LNY) in patients undergoing neck dissection (ND) at the time of wide local excision (WLE) for head and neck cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (HNCSCC). STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study. SETTING: Two academic medical centers. METHODS: Retrospective review of LNY and oncologic outcomes in patients undergoing WLE with ND at two academic centers. RESULTS: A total of 192 total patients who underwent WLE with concurrent ND were included. The cohort was stratified by clinical lymph node status, with half (n = 96) of patients being clinically N+ (cN+) and half (n = 96) of patients being clinically N0 (cN0) at presentation. Total LNY was not predictive of overall survival (OS) when examined as a continuous measure for either group. LNY ≥24 was associated with poorer OS (p = 0.031) and poorer DFS (p = 0.007) for cN0 patients. There was no difference in OS or DFS at any LNY cutoff for cN+ patients on threshold analysis. item.title: Comparison of Survival After Radical Hysterectomy or Radical Radiotherapy Among Patients with Different Histological Types of Locally Advanced Cervical Cancer: Analysis of SEER Data Using Propensity Score Matching.
item.dc:creator: Fan Y, Lian CW, Yang XY, Li JK
item.description:
Authors: Fan Y, Lian CW, Yang XY, Li JK
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18203371
Published: 2026-Oct-18
PMID: 42938903



Abstract:
Objective: To compare survival of patients with different histological types of locally advanced cervical cancer after treatment with radical surgery or radical radiotherapy. Methods: Data for United States residents diagnosed with locally advanced cervical cancer between 2000 and 2022 were extracted from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results database. Overall survival and cancer-specific survival were compared using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. To minimize baseline differences, patients from each group were paired using propensity score matching. Results: Among the 1,363 patients with squamous cell carcinoma in the propensity score-matched cohort, surgery was associated with significantly better overall survival when disease was in stage IB3 (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.50-0.97), but not when it was in other stages. Cancer-specific survival did not differ significantly between the two treatments at any disease stage. Among the 576 patients with adenocarcinoma in the propensity-score-matched cohort, surgery was associated with significantly better overall survival in stages IB3 (HR 0.46, 95% CI 0.28-0.77) or IIA2 (HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.15-0.96) or IIB involving tumors < 4 cm (HR 0.36, 95% CI 0.16-0.80). In the case of adenocarcinoma, surgery may be associated with better overall and cancer-specific survival than radiotherapy in stage IB3 or IIA2 and in stage IIB involving tumors < 4 cm.

item.title: Chloride Channels as Determinants of Anti-Cancer Drug Response: Why the Therapeutic Direction Reverses Between Channels and Between Tissues.
item.dc:creator: Seo Y
item.description:
Authors: Seo Y
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18203369
Published: 2026-Oct-18
PMID: 42938901



Abstract:
Background/Objectives: Resistance to cytotoxic chemotherapy and radiotherapy is usually attributed to DNA repair, drug efflux and apoptotic threshold. Chloride channels intersect these processes but are rarely considered as a group. This review asks whether chloride flux forms a coherent, targetable axis of treatment response and, if not, how the therapeutic direction differs by channel and tissue. Methods: PubMed was searched to 23 August 2026; all free-text searches were re-executed on 22 September 2026 and supplemented by controlled-vocabulary searches. Cited records were checked against NCBI E-utilities and screened for retractions. Claims were graded by whether pharmacological phenotypes were reproduced by genetic perturbation and by the available target-engagement and replication evidence. Results: The therapeutic direction is not uniform. In experimental models, LRRC8A- and LRRC8D-containing channels mediate substantial platinum uptake, and dose-stratified associations between their expression and outcome have been reported in head and neck cancer, supporting prospective evaluation as predictive biomarkers; contrary reports in ovarian, colon and breast models indicate that this direction is established for platinum uptake rather than for cytotoxic resistance in general. CFTR is an intestinal tumour suppressor and the only channel reviewed with an approved potentiator, yet its direction reverses in glioma, with a prostate report of CFTR-dependent cisplatin resistance pointing in the same direction. Conversely, ClC-3, ANO1 and CLIC1 are associated with resistance when gained, although CLIC1 is better supported as a determinant of drug response than of tumorigenesis. Sixteen modulators are compared by potency, assay format, selectivity/counter-screening and clinical status; widely used blockers are often poorly selective. Conclusions: Chloride transport is not a single therapeutic target class. Candidate chloride-channel blockers should be counter-screened against LRRC8/VRAC before combination with platinum therapy, and CFTR potentiation should not be generalised across tumour types. Conflicting evidence is reported alongside the directions it qualifies rather than set aside.

item.title: Giant Keratinocyte Carcinomas: Clinical, Histopathological, Molecular and Health-System Factors with Therapeutic Implications-A Structured Narrative Review.
item.dc:creator: Ciborek A, Krauss H, Chęcińska-Maciejewska Z, Jaworek AK
item.description:
Authors: Ciborek A, Krauss H, Chęcińska-Maciejewska Z, Jaworek AK
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18203367
Published: 2026-Oct-18

Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Giant keratinocyte carcinomas, comprising basal cell carcinoma (BCC) and cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) with a maximum diameter ≥ 5 cm, pose substantial clinical challenges. This structured narrative review distinguishes giant-specific findings from contextual evidence in advanced or high-risk disease. METHODS: The synthesis uses a retained bibliography assembled from searches described in earlier drafts as covering PubMed/MEDLINE and PubMed Central from January 2015 to March 2026, supplemented by citation and guideline searching and a focused update reported through 4 September 2026. A record-level search and screening log is unavailable; historical selection counts cannot be independently reconstructed. The review protocol was not registered, and exhaustive coverage or full PRISMA compliance is not claimed. Sources were classified by design and directness, with descriptive consideration of methodological limitations. RESULTS: The retained set contains 51 sources: nine containing direct giant-specific clinical evidence and 42 providing contextual evidence. Direct evidence consists principally of case reports, retrospective or comparative studies and a giant-cSCC literature synthesis. It links giant BCC with prolonged lesion duration, ulceration, deeper invasion and reconstructive burden. Giant-cSCC outcomes vary substantially between reported series. Evidence for Hedgehog-pathway inhibition, PD-1 blockade and most molecular mechanisms derives mainly from conventional or advanced disease. CONCLUSIONS: Management requires multidisciplinary assessment integrating size, pathological risk, resectability and patient factors. Giant-specific molecular and therapeutic evidence remains limited, and contextual treatment effects should not be interpreted as effects established specifically in tumours ≥ 5 cm.

item.title: Prospective evaluation of combination oral S-1 and intravenous cisplatin in cancer patients with severe hepatic dysfunction - a feasibility, safety, and pharmacokinetic study.
item.dc:creator: Gwee YX, Wong ALA, Goh BC, Soo RA, Yong WP, Tan DSP, Chee CE, Lim SE, Ang Y, Huang Y, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Gwee YX, Wong ALA, Goh BC, Soo RA, Yong WP, Tan DSP, Chee CE, Lim SE, Ang Y, Huang Y, et al.
