Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with advanced solid tumors and severe hepatic dysfunction have limited systemic therapy options due to impaired drug metabolism and increased toxicity risks. This population is often excluded from clinical trials, leaving a critical treatment gap. This study evaluates the feasibility, safety, pharmacokinetics and efficacy of S-1, an oral prodrug of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), plus cisplatin in these patients. METHODS: Between September 2016 and November 2023, 61 patients were enrolled into four cohorts based on hepatic function per NCI-ODWG criteria: normal (Cohort 1), mild (Cohort 2), moderate (Cohort 3), and severe dysfunction (Cohort 4). Primary endpoints were safety and 5-fluorouracil pharmacokinetics; secondary endpoints included objective response rate (ORR) and 3-month clinical benefit rate (3M-CBR). RESULTS: On Cycle 1 day 15, patients with severe hepatic dysfunction (Cohort 4) had lower 5-FU Cmax and longer Tmax than those with normal hepatic function (Cohort 1) (p<0.05), though 5-FU AUC remained comparable across cohorts. Safety in Cohort 4 were similar to those in Cohorts 1-3. No grade 5 treatment-related adverse events occurred. In Cohort 4, 22.2% achieved a partial response, 40.7% derived clinical benefit, and 22.2% maintained progression-free survival ≥6 months, providing preliminary evidence of clinical activity in this population. CONCLUSION: Patients with severe hepatic dysfunction had similar 5-FU AUC and toxicities to those with less severe hepatic dysfunction, and preliminary evidence of clinical activity was observed with cisplatin + S-1. These findings provide prospective preliminary evidence that this combination may be feasible in selected patients with severe hepatic dysfunction, a population frequently excluded from clinical trials. Larger studies are needed to further define its safety, pharmacokinetics, and clinical activity in this population.(Clinical Trial Registration: NCT03519074. Retrospectively registered 08 May 2018).

item.title: Global thyroid cancer incidence in relation to dietary and socioeconomic factors: an ecological machine learning study.
item.dc:creator: Li Y, Liu D, Qin R, Li X, Li M
item.description:
Authors: Li Y, Liu D, Qin R, Li X, Li M
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1842508
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42964100



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thyroid cancer incidence has risen dramatically worldwide, with marked geographic heterogeneity suggesting dietary and environmental contributions beyond screening effects. The roles of specific dietary patterns in thyroid cancer remain poorly characterized at the global level. OBJECTIVES: Age-standardized thyroid cancer incidence was the prespecified primary outcome. We aimed to (1) build machine learning models predicting country-level thyroid cancer incidence from dietary and socioeconomic features, (2) quantify confounder-adjusted dietary associations with incidence, including prespecified sensitivity analyses of the iodine-rich food availability index, and (3) identify key dietary predictors through explainability analyses and a descriptive decomposition of the development pathway. Mortality was analyzed only as a secondary outcome in order to evaluate whether the incidence patterns could be attributed to differential cancer detection rather than to differences in disease occurrence. METHODS: We integrated GLOBOCAN 2022 (cancer outcomes), FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (113 food items, 2010-2022; primary exposure 2015-2019 mean), the UNDP Human Development Report 2025 statistical annex (HDI 2023 and its life expectancy, education, and income sub-indices), and WHO obesity prevalence (2022) across 163 countries, yielding 155 harmonized variables and 150 numeric predictors. All modeling was performed inside a nested cross-validation framework: multiple imputation by chained equations, standardization, four-method consensus feature selection, and hyperparameter search were fitted exclusively on the training partition of each outer fold (10 folds × five repetitions), and performance was summarized from pooled out-of-fold predictions with 95% confidence intervals obtained by resampling countries (2,000 bootstrap replicates). Three analyses separated dietary signal from confounding: block-wise models comparing socioeconomic-only, diet-only and combined feature sets; leave-one-region-out validation across six world regions; and confounder-adjusted partial correlations under a basic (HDI, obesity) and an extended adjustment set (HDI, obesity, the three HDI sub-indices, and region fixed effects), with Benjamini-Hochberg and Bonferroni correction applied across all comparisons. Iodine-related exposure was represented by an iodine-rich food availability index constructed from seafood, dairy, and egg supply; its construction was interrogated in four sensitivity analyses in which the components were entered separately and jointly, four weighting schemes were compared, total animal protein supply was added to the adjustment set, and an iodine-poor animal-origin food index was used as a specificity control. Binary classification and all mortality analyses were secondary. RESULTS: Regression on incidence was the primary task. Stacking ensemble performed best, with a pooled out-of-fold R² of 0.613 (95% CI [0.510, 0.726]), RMSE = 3.04, MAE = 1.82, and Spearman ρ = 0.901 (95% CI [0.862, 0.924]); random forest (R² = 0.609), bagging (R² = 0.599), and KNN (R² = 0.580) followed, and a high-dimensional deep tabular model (DynaTab) was statistically comparable (R² = 0.626). Predictive accuracy was, however, almost entirely socioeconomic: nine development variables alone gave R² = 0.609, 140 dietary variables alone gave 0.284, and the incremental contribution of the dietary block was -0.048 (95% CI -0.169 to +0.034), +0.021, and +0.017 across model families. Under leave-one-region-out validation, the rank ordering of countries was largely preserved (pooled ρ = 0.813), but the level was not. Unadjusted associations with incidence were positive for the iodine-rich food availability index (ρ = 0.234), total energy (ρ = 0.230), seafood (ρ = 0.219), and the animal-to-plant protein ratio (ρ = 0.221). After adjustment and Benjamini-Hochberg correction, seafood supply, dairy supply, the iodine-rich food availability index, the animal-to-plant protein ratio, and mollusks remained significant under the extended adjustment set (seafood partial r = 0.196, q = 0.031; iodine-rich food availability index 0.224, q = 0.026), whereas plant protein did not (-0.095, q = 0.309). In sensitivity analyses, the index association was carried by seafood (0.196, q = 0.017) and dairy (0.198, q = 0.017) but not eggs (0.065, q = 0.411), was stable across equal-weighted, z-score, and iodine-content-weighted constructions (0.238-0.256), survived further adjustment for total animal protein supply (0.203, q = 0.032), and was not reproduced by an iodine-poor animal-origin food index (0.102, q = 0.198). Path decomposition attributed 50.2% of the seafood-incidence correlation to the HDI pathway (95% bootstrap CI 16%-90%). In the secondary mortality analysis, the dietary ordering was preserved, but associations with the mortality-to-incidence ratio were close to zero (HDI ρ = 0.053; seafood ρ = 0.065), and in the sensitivity classification analysis, Extra Trees reached AUC = 0.932 (95% CI [0.893, 0.964]) at the median split. CONCLUSIONS: With all model construction confined to training folds, machine learning models built from national food supply and socioeconomic data explain a moderate share of the between-country variation in thyroid cancer incidence, but that predictive accuracy is carried by development indicators rather than by diet. The availability of iodine-rich food groups, seafood supply, and the animal-to-plant protein ratio nevertheless retained positive ecological associations with incidence after adjustment for development and metabolic confounders and after correction for multiple comparisons, and the index association proved robust to how the index was constructed and specific to iodine-rich rather than to animal-origin food groups in general; plant protein showed no association once multiplicity was controlled. Roughly half of the seafood-incidence correlation tracks the development pathway, and the secondary mortality analysis is consistent with a substantial contribution from differential detection. These findings are ecological associations with the availability of iodine-rich food groups, not with measured iodine intake or exposure; they generate testable hypotheses for individual-level studies with measured iodine status and do not establish causation.

item.title: Postoperative ctDNA could potentially spare patients from unnecessary adjuvant therapy in HPV-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a meta-analysis.
item.dc:creator: Asad MR, Pusarico AF, Reji N, AlRamadneh TN, Khan AU
item.description:
Authors: Asad MR, Pusarico AF, Reji N, AlRamadneh TN, Khan AU
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1902328
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42964065



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic utility of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) for minimal residual disease detection in human papillomavirus (HPV)-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) remains incompletely characterized. This meta-analysis evaluates the association between post-operative ctDNA and recurrence-free survival (RFS) in this population. METHODS: A systematic search of major databases through May 2026 identified studies evaluating post-operative ctDNA and RFS in HPV-negative HNSCC. Pooled hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated using a random-effects model. RESULTS: Eight studies (n=325) were included. Detectable post-operative ctDNA was associated with diminished RFS (HR = 10.07, 95% CI: 5.64-17.99) and overall survival (HR = 8.98, 95% CI: 2.93-27.58). However, sensitivity analyses substantially attenuated the pooled RFS estimate (HR range: 2.22-2.43), suggesting the primary effect magnitude may lack stability. CONCLUSIONS: While preliminary evidence suggests an association between post-operative ctDNA and recurrence risk in HPV-negative HNSCC, these findings require cautious interpretation. The current literature is constrained by small sample sizes, heterogeneous detection methodologies, mixed-cohort inclusion, and potential confounding biases. Consequently, post-operative ctDNA remains an investigational biomarker in this setting. Clinical implementation necessitates further validation through large, prospective, multi-institutional studies employing standardized methodologies in strictly defined HPV-negative #146;populations.

item.title: The Evolution of Neoadjuvant Treatment for Resectable Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Past Achievements, Current Standards, and Future Perspectives.
item.dc:creator: Ujiie N, Taniyama Y, Sato C, Okamoto H, Ozawa Y, Ishida H, Unno M, Kamei T
item.description:
Authors: Ujiie N, Taniyama Y, Sato C, Okamoto H, Ozawa Y, Ishida H, Unno M, Kamei T
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18203350
Published: 2026-Oct-16
PMID: 42938882



Abstract:
Neoadjuvant treatment has become an integral component of multidisciplinary management for resectable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). Over recent decades, treatment has evolved from surgery alone to postoperative chemotherapy, neoadjuvant chemotherapy, intensified systemic therapy, neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy, and, more recently, the incorporation of immune checkpoint inhibitors into curative-intent treatment. This evolution has been driven by persistent challenges including systemic recurrence, locoregional failure, treatment-related toxicity, and heterogeneous treatment response. This review traces the evolution of neoadjuvant treatment for resectable ESCC through landmark clinical trials that have shaped current practice. We discuss the transition from postoperative to neoadjuvant chemotherapy, the development of intensified chemotherapy and neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy, and the emergence of immunotherapy, distinguishing the established role of adjuvant nivolumab from the emerging role of neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy. We then examine the unresolved relative roles of these strategies and the challenges in treatment selection. Finally, we discuss future directions centered on accurate response assessment, circulating tumor DNA-based molecular residual disease assessment, and response-adapted treatment, with particular emphasis on organ-preserving strategies after a clinical complete response. Although active surveillance has emerged as a potential alternative to immediate surgery in carefully selected patients, accurate identification of residual disease and appropriate surveillance remain essential. Future advances may therefore shift the focus from treatment intensification alone toward response-adapted strategies that can maintain oncological safety while potentially enabling organ preservation.

item.title: Prophylactic pirfenidone to prevent radiation- induced lung injury in ICI-pretreated lung cancer patients: a phase II study.
item.dc:creator: Huang Y, Ma J, Han G, Bi J, Pi G, Li Y, Peng Y, Xiao C, Tuo X
item.description:
Authors: Huang Y, Ma J, Han G, Bi J, Pi G, Li Y, Peng Y, Xiao C, Tuo X
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1876642
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42959154



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to relieve radiation-induced lung injury (RILI) by assessing the use of prophylactic pirfenidone. Subjects were lung cancer patients with prior ICI treatment who received thoracic radiotherapy. METHODS: Patients with lung cancer were enrolled in this phase II single-arm study. All candidates had a history of prior ICI exposure (≥2 cycles; interval ≤6 months) scheduled for thoracic radiotherapy (≥50 Gy). Patients received oral pirfenidone (1800 mg/day) from one week pre-radiotherapy to four weeks post-completion. The primary endpoint was the 6-month incidence of ≥grade 2 RILI, compared to a 40% historical control (p0=0.40; p1=0.22; α=0.10; power=80%). Secondary endpoints included pulmonary function (DLCO%, FVC%) and safety. RESULTS: A total of 39 patients were enrolled in this trial. At the 6-month follow-up, the incidence of grade 2 or higher RILI was 23.1% (9/39; 95% CI: 11.1%-39.3%). This rate was statistically significantly lower than the 40% incidence from the historical control cohort (p=0.0205). Grade 3 RILI occurred in 7.7% (3/39); no grade 4-5 events occurred. Mean DLCO% declined by 7.6 ± 5.4% at 3 months and 6.5 ± 5.8% at 6 months. The pirfenidone completion rate was 84.6% (median relative dose intensity: 89.3%). Common adverse events were fatigue (43.6%), nausea (41.0%), and appetite loss (33.3%), mostly grade 1-2. CONCLUSIONS: Preventive use of pirfenidone was associated with a lower observed incidence and severity of RILI than the predefined historical control in ICI-pretreated lung cancer patients receiving thoracic radiotherapy. Additionally, the intervention showed a potential protective trend for pulmonary diffusion function. These findings require further validation in a phase III trial.

item.title: Radiologist-guided multimodal fusion network for differentiating parotid tumors on 3D non-contrast CT.
item.dc:creator: Yang Q, Liao W, Sun J, Mu D, Yang M, Li Q, Zhao Y, Zhang S
item.description:
Authors: Yang Q, Liao W, Sun J, Mu D, Yang M, Li Q, Zhao Y, Zhang S
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1926379
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42959120



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To improve the diagnostic accuracy of benign versus malignant parotid tumors using non-contrast CT. We propose a clinician-in-the-loop hybrid framework that mitigates low soft-tissue contrast by fusing semi-automated 3D visual features with expert semantic descriptors. METHODS: This multi-center retrospective study analyzed non-contrast CTs from 367 patients. We developed AttenNet, a semi-automated model. First, an nnU-Net module automates 3D tumor segmentation, eliminating manual bounding boxes. A 3D-ResNet backbone then extracts volumetric features, which are dynamically fused with radiologist-provided semantic labels via a Multi-Head Cross-Attention Fusion (MHAF) mechanism. This allows the network to query visual morphology based on expert priors. Diagnostic performance and Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) interpretability were evaluated. RESULTS: The segmentation achieved a median Dice of 0.827. AttenNet (3D-ResNet) yielded an AUC of 0.908, significantly outperforming the image-only 3D-ResNet (AUC: 0.741) and expert-feature models (AUC: 0.821). External validation (n = 20) reached an AUC of 0.560-0.910.However, given the extremely small sample size, these results must be interpreted strictly as an exploratory proof-of-concept rather than definitive confirmation of generalizability. Grad-CAM confirmed that AttenNet highlights clinically essential geometric indicators-specifically tumor margins and internal heterogeneity-for differentiating malignancy, whereas single-modality baselines focused on background artifacts. CONCLUSION: This clinician-in-the-loop paradigm successfully integrates spatial imaging with expert reasoning. While multimodal fusion drove the primary performance gains, the MHAF mechanism provided enhanced spatial interpretability.

item.title: Changing epidemiology and survival of HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer in Denmark: four decades of population-based data.
item.dc:creator: Jakobsen KK, Jensen JM, Hansen J, von Buchwald C, Grønhøj C
item.description:
Authors: Jakobsen KK, Jensen JM, Hansen J, von Buchwald C, Grønhøj C
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1982354
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42959054



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) has undergone substantial epidemiological and clinical changes, with an increasing proportion of human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated tumours and declining tobacco exposure. We investigated temporal changes in patient characteristics, HPV/p16 status, treatment patterns, and survival among patients with OPSCC in Denmark. METHODS: Patients with OPSCC were identified from the Copenhagen Oropharyngeal Cancer Database (2000-2023) and the Danish National Patient Cancer Registry (DCR; 1980-2021). The Copenhagen database provided detailed clinical and pathological data, including HPV/p16 status, while the DCR enabled assessment of long-term survival trends. Temporal changes were evaluated across diagnostic periods. Overall survival, relative survival, and restricted mean survival time were estimated. RESULTS: Among 3,631 OPSCC patients in the Copenhagen database, median age at diagnosis increased from 59 years in 2000-2005 to 64 years in 2018-2023 (p<0.001). The proportion of HPV+/p16+ patients increased significantly from 43.5% in 2000-2005 to 62.8% in 2018-2023. The proportion of never smokers also increased from 0.5% to 23.5%, while ≥20 pack-years decreased from 73.2% to 52.1% (p<0.001). Treatment patterns changed substantially, with radiotherapy alone decreasing from 87.6% to 27.9% and chemoradiotherapy increasing from 1.6% to 46.3%. Among 9,379 patients in the DCR, five-year relative survival increased from 31.8% in 1980-1984 to 70.1% in 2015-2019. Among HPV+/p16+ patients, five-year overall survival increased from 63.1% in 2000-2005 to 83.7% in 2018-2023. CONCLUSION: In Denmark, OPSCC has undergone substantial epidemiological and therapeutic changes accompanied by marked improvements in survival, including among HPV+/p16+ patients.

item.title: Surgical Timing in Relation to Visual Dysfunction in Skull Base Meningiomas Involving the Anterior Visual Pathway: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
item.dc:creator: Kawamata T, Eguchi S, Morita S, Yamaguchi K, Amano K
item.description:
Authors: Kawamata T, Eguchi S, Morita S, Yamaguchi K, Amano K
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18203324
Published: 2026-Oct-15
PMID: 42938859



Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Observation is generally recommended for asymptomatic meningiomas, but evidence from incidental meningiomas is derived largely from heterogeneous intracranial locations and may not directly apply to tumors involving the anterior visual pathway. We investigated whether preoperative visual status remained associated with postoperative visual function after adjustment for baseline clinical and anatomical differences in this location-specific subgroup. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 146 patients who underwent resection of skull base meningiomas contacting or compressing the optic nerve and/or chiasm. Preoperative visual status was categorized by comprehensive ophthalmologic evaluation as normal visual function or visual dysfunction. The primary outcome was postoperative normal visual function, defined as preservation of normal vision in patients with normal preoperative visual function and complete recovery in those with preoperative visual dysfunction. Multivariable logistic regression was performed, and propensity score matching was conducted using age, sex, tumor volume, tumor laterality, and optic canal involvement. RESULTS: Propensity score matching yielded 48 matched pairs with adequate balance across all measured covariates (all standardized mean differences < 0.1). Postoperative normal visual function was preserved or achieved in 95.8% of patients with normal preoperative visual function versus 31.3% of those with preoperative visual dysfunction (exact McNemar p < 0.001). Favorable visual outcome occurred in 95.8% versus 77.1%, respectively (p = 0.0225). CONCLUSIONS: Among surgically treated patients, normal preoperative visual function remained strongly associated with postoperative normal visual function after adjustment for measured clinical and anatomical differences. These findings do not establish that earlier surgery improves visual outcomes or define an optimal surgical timing strategy, but suggest that preoperative visual status and tumor anatomy should be considered in individualized management decisions.

item.title: Multimodal radiomics based on dynamic contrast-enhanced ultrasound for predicting cervical lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma with Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
item.dc:creator: Zhang K, Zhao D, Wang G, Gu Y, Wu X, Dong F
item.description:
Authors: Zhang K, Zhao D, Wang G, Gu Y, Wu X, Dong F
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1840185
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42952523



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and validate a multimodal predictive model by integrating radiomic features from B-mode ultrasound (BMUS) and dynamic contrast-enhanced ultrasound (DCE-US) parametric imaging, as well as clinical and conventional ultrasound features, for preoperative prediction of cervical lymph node metastasis (CLNM) in patients with Hashimoto's thyroiditis (HT) complicated with papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). METHODS: A total of 191 patients with pathologically confirmed HT-complicated PTC were retrospectively enrolled between December 2023 and July 2025. Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n=133) and a validation set (n=58) at a 7:3 ratio using a random number generator. Radiomic features were extracted from BMUS images and DCE-US peak enhancement parametric maps. Feature stability was assessed using intraclass and interclass correlation coefficients (ICC). Key features were selected through a sequential process including the Mann-Whitney U test, recursive feature elimination (RFE), and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, followed by calculation of the radiomics score (Rad-score). Independent predictors of CLNM were identified using multivariate logistic regression incorporating clinical and ultrasound features. Three predictive models were constructed: a clinical-ultrasound model, a radiomics model, and a combined multi-modal model. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Model interpretability was enhanced using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis. RESULTS: TG-Ab, TR-Ab, extrathyroidal extension, filling defects, BMUS Rad-score, and DCE-US Rad-score were independent predictors of CLNM (P < 0.05). In the training and validation sets, the combined model achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.936 and 0.916, respectively, which were significantly higher than those of the radiomics model (AUC = 0.825, 0.876) and the clinical-ultrasound model (AUC = 0.760, 0.800; DeLong test, P < 0.05). Calibration curves showed good model fitting. DCA confirmed that the combined model provided greater clinical net benefit. NRI and IDI verified that the combined model significantly improved CLNM prediction performance. SHAP analysis revealed that DCE-US Rad-score was the most important predictor for CLNM. CONCLUSION: A multi-modal predictive model combining dual-modality ultrasound radiomic scores (BMUS and DCE-US) with clinical and ultrasound features can effectively and robustly predict CLNM in patients with HT-complicated PTC and performs better than single-modal models. This model provides an objective reference for the formulation of individualized surgical strategies.

item.title: An Exploratory Study of ABT-806, a Tumor-Specific Anti-EGFR Antibody, in Subjects with Recurrent or Metastatic Head and Neck and Other Squamous Cell Carcinomas.
item.dc:creator: Gan HK, Parakh S, Ameratunga M, Hamid A, Iatropoulos G, Beecher M, Cao D, Westcott K, Caine J, Palmer J, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Gan HK, Parakh S, Ameratunga M, Hamid A, Iatropoulos G, Beecher M, Cao D, Westcott K, Caine J, Palmer J, et al.
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18203313
Published: 2026-Oct-14
PMID: 42938848



Abstract:
Introduction: Despite their benefit, current anti-EGFR therapies are limited by narrow efficacy profiles due to dose-limiting toxicities. This phase 2 open-label study evaluated the efficacy and safety of ABT-806, an EGFR-targeting antibody that is tumor specific, in patients with advanced EGFR-expressing tumors including head and neck cancers (H&NC) and squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) of other sites. Methods: Patients with advanced H&NC (cohort A) or SCC of other sites (cohort B) were enrolled in the study. ABT-806 was administered as monotherapy at a dose of 24 mg/kg intravenously using a twice weekly dosing schedule until unacceptable toxicity and/or evidence of disease progression. Adverse events (AEs) were graded using the National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events v4.0; tumor response was assessed using the Response Evaluation criteria in Solid Tumors v1.1. EGFR status was assessed with mAb806 and EGFRvIII immunohistochemistry and correlated with outcomes. Results: ABT-806 was well tolerated with no grade 3+ treatment-related AEs. Disease stabilization was observed in two patients (14%) and for a median duration of 19.5 weeks. This included one patient from cohort A and one patient from cohort B. Progression-free survival and overall survival was not significantly different between the two cohorts. Conclusions: Although clinical activity was limited in this small, heavily pre-treated, and biomarker-unselected population, ABT-806 demonstrated an excellent safety profile with minimal classical EGFR-related toxicity. These findings support the development of more tumor-specific EGFR antibodies for use, particularly in combinatorial regimens.

item.title: Minimally Invasive Versus Open CRS/HIPEC for Peritoneal Surface Malignancies: Postoperative Recovery and Long-Term Outcomes-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.dc:creator: Aulicino M, Tondolo V, Abatini C, D'Annibale G, Barberis L, Saiz M, Fiorillo C, De Sio D, Quero G, Alfieri S, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Aulicino M, Tondolo V, Abatini C, D'Annibale G, Barberis L, Saiz M, Fiorillo C, De Sio D, Quero G, Alfieri S, et al.
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18203310
Published: 2026-Oct-14
PMID: 42938846



Abstract:
Background: Minimally invasive surgery (MIS) is increasingly implemented for cytoreductive surgery (CRS) combined with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) for peritoneal surface malignancies (PSM). This systematic review and meta-analysis compared minimally invasive CRS/HIPEC (M-CRS/HIPEC) and open CRS/HIPEC (O-CRS/HIPEC) in terms of perioperative, postoperative, and long-term oncological outcomes. Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for comparative studies of M-CRS/HIPEC versus O-CRS/HIPEC in adult patients. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and RoB 2.0. Pooled relative risks (RR) for dichotomous outcomes and standardized mean differences (SMD) for continuous outcomes were calculated with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Sensitivity analyses were performed to assess the potential influence of disease burden and primary tumor heterogeneity. Results: Twenty-one studies (1 randomized controlled trial and 20 retrospective cohorts) including 1184 patients (452 M-CRS/HIPEC and 732 O-CRS/HIPEC) were analyzed. Operative time did not differ between groups (SMD = 0.195; p = 0.667). Most cytoreductive procedures were comparable, although small bowel resections were less frequent with M-CRS/HIPEC (RR = 0.537; p = 0.018). The minimally invasive approach achieved higher CC0 rates (RR = 1.053; p = 0.045), with lower blood loss (SMD = -1.838; p < 0.001) and fewer transfusions (RR = 0.588; p = 0.002). Postoperative recovery favored M-CRS/HIPEC, with earlier return of bowel function and resumption of oral intake, shorter hospital stay, fewer readmissions, and earlier chemotherapy resumption (all p < 0.05). Overall and major morbidity were reduced, while postoperative mortality and 1-, 3-, and 5-year disease-free and overall survival did not differ significantly between groups. In the disease burden-restricted sensitivity analysis, differences in small bowel resection, CC0 rate, and 90-day readmission were no longer statistically significant, whereas the main perioperative and recovery benefits persisted. No significant differences in DFS or OS were identified in the additional sensitivity analyses at the evaluable time points. Conclusions: This meta-analysis supports a selective, expertise-driven use of M-CRS/HIPEC, offering perioperative and recovery advantages without significant differences in cytoreductive adequacy or long-term outcomes in appropriately selected patients.

item.title: Retrospective Analysis of Efficacy and Toxicity of Low-Dose Weekly Cisplatin Concurrently with Radiotherapy for p16-Positive Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Niranjan N, Otty Z, Joshi A, Hu M, Edkins O, Deacon S, Fisher C, Brown A, Ryan C, Bain N, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Niranjan N, Otty Z, Joshi A, Hu M, Edkins O, Deacon S, Fisher C, Brown A, Ryan C, Bain N, et al.
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18203308
Published: 2026-Oct-14
PMID: 42938844



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence of p16-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is increasing, with improved prognosis compared to non-HPV-related cancers. Standard treatment of locally advanced OPSCC involves high-dose cisplatin (HDC) with radiation but is associated with significant toxicity. Low-dose cisplatin (LDC) administered weekly has shown comparable efficacy to HDC in prior studies. This study evaluates the real-world outcomes of LDC in p16-positive OPSCC in a regional centre. MATERIAL AND METHODS: Patients treated with curative radiation and concurrent LDC (40 mg/m2 weekly) for p16-positive OPSCC from January 2015 to December 2021 were retrospectively analysed (n = 103). Primary endpoints included overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS), with secondary endpoints being loco-regional and distant recurrence rates, and chemotherapy-related toxicity. RESULTS: Overall survival rates were 94%, 89%, and 84% at two, three, and five years, respectively. The progression-free survival rates were 90%, 83%, and 80% over the same periods. The low-risk group showed excellent outcomes with no loco-regional recurrences and low distant relapse rates (6% at 5 years). The intermediate-risk group had higher loco-regional recurrences (10% at 5 years) and a similar distant relapse rate (7% at 5 years). T4 or N3 disease patients had lower survival and higher distant relapse rates but excellent loco-regional control. The median cumulative cisplatin dose was 240 mg/m2, with no survival difference between those receiving ≥200 mg/m2 versus less. Toxicity led to dose reductions (8%), delays (13%), and early cessations (30%). CONCLUSIONS: LDC is effective for p16-positive OPSCC with manageable toxicity, showing outcomes comparable to outcomes previously reported in studies using HDC.

item.title: Malignant potential of oral lichen planus without epithelial dysplasia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of longitudinal studies.
item.dc:creator: Domingues CB, Botelho J, Azul AM, Trancoso PF
item.description:
Authors: Domingues CB, Botelho J, Azul AM, Trancoso PF
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1949729
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42947806



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Oral lichen planus (OLP) is a chronic inflammatory disease of the oral mucosa classified as a potentially malignant oral disease. However, its risk of malignant transformation remains controversial because of heterogeneous diagnostic criteria and methodologies across studies. OBJECTIVE: To assess the malignant transformation rate of non-dysplastic OLP through a systematic review and meta-analysis of longitudinal studies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261295782). PubMed, Embase, and grey literature were searched. Longitudinal observational studies including patients with histopathologically diagnosed OLP, without epithelial dysplasia at diagnosis, and reporting malignant transformation rates were included. The review focused specifically on longitudinal evidence evaluating malignant transformation in patients meeting these eligibility criteria. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and meta-analysis was performed using a random-effects model. RESULTS: Twenty-four studies, comprising 13, 143 patients and 230 cases of malignant transformation, were included. The pooled malignant transformation rate was 1.56% (95% CI: 1.14-2.12%), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 74.8%). Subgroup analyses showed no significant differences according to study design, geographic region, or diagnostic criteria. Meta-regression identified the male-to-female ratio as a significant moderator, while sample size and follow-up duration had no significant influence. No evidence of publication bias was observed. CONCLUSIONS: The malignant transformation rate of OLP was very low, with a pooled estimate of 1.56%, supporting continued surveillance. Future research should focus on standardized diagnostic approaches and reliable risk stratification models to improve understanding of malignant transformation in OLP and ensure better population representation. item.title: CNIH4 as a prognostic biomarker and promoter of malignant progression in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Chen J, Nai A, Cai J, Liao M, Lu S, He J
item.description:
Authors: Chen J, Nai A, Cai J, Liao M, Lu S, He J
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1963295
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42947760



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is a molecularly heterogeneous malignancy with variable clinical outcomes. Although cornichon family AMPA receptor auxiliary protein 4 (CNIH4) has been implicated in several disease processes, its clinical and biological relevance in HNSCC remains incompletely defined. METHODS: Transcriptomic, genomic, and clinical data from The Cancer Genome Atlas and independent Gene Expression Omnibus cohorts were integrated for bioinformatic analyses. CNIH4 expression was evaluated in relation to diagnostic performance, clinicopathological features, survival, somatic mutations, tumor mutation burden, immune infiltration, immune-regulatory genes, and drug-response profiles. A prognostic nomogram incorporating CNIH4 was also assessed. Functional studies were performed in SAS and SCC-9 oral squamous cell carcinoma cells using two independent CNIH4-targeting siRNAs. Proliferation, colony formation, and wound closure were measured, followed by RNA sequencing and pathway analyses after CNIH4 knockdown. RESULTS: CNIH4 was consistently overexpressed in HNSCC and validated in three independent cohorts, with retrospective discrimination between tumor and normal tissues in the TCGA-HNSC transcriptomic dataset (AUC = 0.915). Higher CNIH4 expression was associated with unfavorable clinicopathological features and shorter overall survival, disease-specific survival, disease-free interval, and progression-free interval. The nomogram showed moderate prognostic performance, with AUCs of 0.710, 0.750, and 0.720 at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. CNIH4 expression was also associated with distinct mutation patterns, higher tumor mutation burden, and differences in bulk transcriptome-derived immune and stromal signatures and immune-regulatory gene expression. Higher CNIH4 expression correlated with lower predicted IC50 values for fluorouracil, tegafur, paclitaxel, and nilotinib. Experimentally, CNIH4 depletion reduced proliferation, colony formation, and wound closure in both cell lines. RNA sequencing revealed changes involving epithelial-mesenchymal transition, interferon signaling, TNF-α/NF-κB signaling, NOTCH signaling, p53-related programs, and the unfolded protein response. CONCLUSIONS: This study suggests that CNIH4 is associated with HNSCC progression-related phenotypes and clinical outcomes. Functional and transcriptomic findings support a functional association between CNIH4 and malignant phenotypes in oral squamous cell carcinoma and justify further investigation of its prognostic and therapeutic relevance in HNSCC.

item.title: Comparative effectiveness of neoadjuvant treatment strategies and predictors of pathological complete response in locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: a real-world retrospective cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Yuan X, Liang Y, Han T, Guo Z, Sun Y, Dong Y, Zhang L, Li H, Li J, Sun X, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Yuan X, Liang Y, Han T, Guo Z, Sun Y, Dong Y, Zhang L, Li H, Li J, Sun X, et al.
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1916194
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42947675



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare pathological complete response (pCR) across different neoadjuvant treatment strategies in patients with locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and to identify clinicopathological factors associated with pCR. METHODS: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 247 consecutive patients with locally advanced ESCC who underwent neoadjuvant therapy followed by radical esophagectomy between January 2024 and June 2025 were included. Patients were categorized into four treatment groups: chemotherapy alone (CT, n = 50), chemoradiotherapy (CRT, n = 38), chemotherapy plus immunotherapy (CT+IO, n = 142), and chemoradiotherapy plus immunotherapy (CRT+IO, n = 17). Pathological complete response was defined as ypT0N0. Clinicopathological characteristics were compared using χ² or Fisher's exact tests. Factors associated with pCR were evaluated using univariable and multivariable logistic regression analysis. RESULTS: Overall, 63 patients (25.5%) achieved pCR. The pCR rate was lower in the CT group than in the CT+IO group (6.0% vs. 26.8%). After adjustment for potential confounders, chemotherapy alone remained associated with lower odds of pCR than CT+IO (OR = 0.174, 95% CI, 0.046-0.658, P = 0.010). No significant differences were observed between CT+IO and either CRT or CRT+IO. Receipt of more than two neoadjuvant treatment cycles was associated with higher odds of pCR (OR = 2.764, 95% CI, 1.372-5.565, P = 0.004). Compared with cT3 disease, cT2 disease was associated with higher odds of pCR (OR = 3.049, 95% CI, 1.356-6.857, P = 0.007). CONCLUSIONS: Neoadjuvant treatment regimen, the number of neoadjuvant treatment cycles, and pretreatment clinical T stage were associated with pathological complete response in locally advanced ESCC. Chemotherapy alone was associated with lower odds of pCR than CT+IO, whereas receipt of more than two treatment cycles was associated with higher odds of pCR. These findings provide real-world evidence regarding factors associated with pathological response.

item.title: Unveiling the heterogeneity: PD-L1 expression and metabolic activity in primary vs. metastatic NSCLC, a retrospective single-center analysis.
item.dc:creator: Hu B, Jin H, Yu Y, Zhang J, You Y, Fu C, Xuan A, Wu X, Gao Y
item.description:
Authors: Hu B, Jin H, Yu Y, Zhang J, You Y, Fu C, Xuan A, Wu X, Gao Y
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1966803
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42947673



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression was different in primary tumors (PT) and metastatic tumors (MT). Total-body positron-emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) comprehensively visualizes primary lesions and metastases. We aimed to explore the heterogeneity of PD-L1 high expression and metabolic activity between primary and metastatic lesions in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). METHODS: Immunohistochemistry analysis (IHC) was conducted for PD-L1 expression on tumor cells (TC) and tumor-infiltrating immune cells (IC) with 22C3 antibody. PD-L1 positive scores on TC no less than 50% or IC no less than 10% was defined as high expression. Total 598 (456 adenocarcinoma (ADC) and 142 squamous cell lung carcinoma (SCC)) primary diagnosed NSCLC patients who underwent 18F-FDG-PET/CT imaging were collected retrospectively. The statistic methods included chi-square test, Mann Whitney test and multivariate regression. RESULTS: 598 patients included 441 with PD-L1 low expression and 157 high expression. In all subtypes and ADC, MT had higher PD-L1 high expression (P = 0.023 and P = 0.010, respectively). The maximum standard uptake value (SUVmax) of PD-L1 high expression was significantly higher than that of PD-L1 low expression, no matter in PT or MT (15.23 (8.85) vs 9.42 (8.34), P<0.001; 13.36 (5.55) vs 8.52 (6.93), P<0.001). The squamous-cell-carcinoma metastatic-lesion analyses were exploratory owing to the very small sample size and risk of type-II statistical error. Multivariate regression indicated that SUVmax was independently associated with PD-L1 high expression. In all metastatic sites, we compared the SUVmax of MT and paired PT and found SUVmax was higher in PT than MT in PD-L1 low expression subgroup (11.39 (8.12) vs 8.52 (6.93), P = 0.002). For lymph node metastases, SUVmax was significantly elevated in PT compared to MT in PD-L1 low expression (13.71 (7.95) vs 8.54 (7.30), P = 0.002), whereas no correlation was observed in PD-L1 high expression. DISCUSSION: Both PD-L1 expression and metabolism exhibited heterogeneity between primary tumors and their metastases. Compared to the primary tumors, different types of metastatic tumors showed variations not only in PD-L1 expression but also in their metabolic parameter. Utilizing whole-body PET/CT imaging facilitates the selection of optimal biopsy sites by providing metabolic reference data pertinent to clinical practice.

item.title: Baseline growth kinetics of pulmonary metastases in head and neck adenoid cystic carcinoma: analysis of correlated clinical and molecular factors.
item.dc:creator: Liu HF, Jiang LY, Ma TY, Zhao Y, Li TY, Wang XL, Zhang SJ, Yang GL, Zhou J, Yan ZY, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Liu HF, Jiang LY, Ma TY, Zhao Y, Li TY, Wang XL, Zhang SJ, Yang GL, Zhou J, Yan ZY, et al.
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1811232
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42935745



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To establish baseline growth rates of lung nodules in untreated head and neck adenoid cystic carcinoma(ACC) patients and analyze associated clinical and molecular factors influencing these rates. METHODS: CT was used to calculate the diameter of 74 pulmonary metastatic nodules in 37 patients under natural state. The diameter growth rate of lung metastatic nodules was fitted with a linear regression equation, and the differences in the progression rate of lung metastasis among patients were compared. Additionally, clinical features such as location, pathological subtypes, and staging were also collected to compare their correlation with the growth rate of lung metastatic nodules. Subsequently, single-cell sequencing data from three lung metastatic nodules of differing diameters within the same case were analyzed. RESULTS: We defined three different states based on the progression of lung metastases: rapid progression was defined as a monthly diameter increase of more than 1 mm in 16.2% (6/37) of the patients; slow progression was defined as a monthly diameter increase between 0.3-1 mm in 56.8% (21/37) of the patients; and stable state was defined as a monthly diameter increase of less than 0.3 mm in 27.0% (10/37) of the patients. In addition, factors such as low expression of TP63, a higher pathological grade (Grade III), and a nodule diameter greater than 10mm at initial diagnosis of lung metastasis were identified as significant predictors for a faster diameter growth rate (P<0.05). Subsequently, through single-cell sequencing analysis, it was found that rapidly progressing nodules exhibited upregulation of signals related to hypoxia, vascular genesis, and a weakening of immune response-related signals. CONCLUSION: The findings of this study suggest that baseline characteristics based on the growth rate of pulmonary metastatic nodules may be used to help stratify the progression rate of lung metastasis. In particular, based on our observations, for patients with pulmonary metastatic lesions presenting with a nodule diameter > 10 mm, pathological grade III, and low TP63 expression at initial diagnosis, clinicians might consider adopting closer follow-up monitoring or potentially initiating intervention measures earlier. Additionally, for rapidly growing pulmonary metastatic nodules, it may be worth considering targeted therapy against hypoxic/anti-angiogenic pathways or combination with immunotherapy aimed at restoring or enhancing local immune responses.
